item.title: Lazio pull clear at Serie A summit
item.description: Lazio forward Andrea Pinamonti celebrates after scoring his team's second goal (tiziana fabi) Gennaro Gattuso's Lazio consolidated their position at the top of Serie A on Sunday with a 2-1 victory over Cagliari, nudging ahead of Inter Milan after the two clubs had started the weekend level on points. Lazio made a poor start as Cagliari took the lead through M'Bala Nzola in the 20th minute before goals in either half from Gustav Isaksen and Andrea Pinamonti gave them a sixth straight Serie A win. With 28 points from 10 games, Lazio moved three clear of Inter after they lost the Milan derby. Unbeaten Roma sit third on 24 points and Como climbed back to fourth with a 1-0 win over rock-bottom Venezia. Lazio last won Serie A in 2000 and this is the best start to a league campaign in the club's history. As has been the case in recent home matches, Lazio played in front of largely empty sections of the Stadio Olimpico, with many ultras and supporters continuing their boycott in protest against owner and president Claudio Lotito, whom they accuse of failing to invest sufficiently in the squad. Como's victory at home over lowly Venezia on Sunday was a fifth consecutive victory across all competitions. The hosts dominated, but needed a penalty to find the back of the net. Como captain Lucas Da Cunha converted in the 43rd minute for the French international's first goal of the season. "This is the type of match we found hard to win last season," Da Cunha told DAZN. Cesc Fabregas's side had slipped to fifth when AC Milan beat champions Inter 3-1 on Saturday. Como moved one point behind Roma, who beat Udinese 5-2 on Saturday. "This victory is really important in terms of our maturing process," said Fabregas. "Our state of mind is irreproachable," added the 39-year-old Spaniard. Como resume their Champions League campaign against Lens on Wednesday. In a season in which Italian teams have struggled in Europe, Como have the best record of the Serie A clubs in the Champions League, sitting ninth in the 36-team standings, with six points from three games. Como, who were playing in Italy's third division as recently as 2021, beat Manchester United 4-1 in the last round of European matches. jr/dmc/mw

item.title: Liverpool v Arsenal: Premier League – live
item.description: Updates from the match at Anfield (4.30pm GMT) Table | Top scorers | Email Daniel here So where is the game? Liverpool will look to get men around the ball when Arsenal have it, opening the pitch for switches should they win possession. And when they don’t, they’ll run like mad to recover it, stretching play and passing forwards, facilitating that by conserving energy every now and again when Nyoni slows the game down. In particular, I expect they’ll ask Bradley Barcola to target the space left when Riccardo Calafiori goes off on adventures, with Alexander Isak pulling away for cut-backs and shooting quickly with little backlift, while Florian Wirtz looks to slip passes in behind – if he can work quickly enough in the maelstrom of the match. Continue reading...

item.title: Is NASCAR’s Championship Format Broken? Kyle Larson’s Title Run Has Fans Questioning Everything
item.description: USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect Kyle Larson is closing in on another NASCAR Cup Series championship, but the numbers behind his title campaign have reignited the debate over whether the playoff format truly rewards the best driver of the season. According to data shared by Pit by Numbers , Larson has recorded four crashes, a 14.7 average finish and lost 20 head-to-head battles against Denny Hamlin across 34 races. Hamlin, meanwhile, has zero DNFs and a 9.1 average finish, the best in the Cup Series. Despite that contrast, Larson holds a 73-point championship advantage with two races remaining. At first glance, it looks like a clear argument against the current format. But there is another side to the numbers. Larson’s Lap-Leading Advantage Changes the Argument Oct 31, 2026; Martinsville, Virginia, USA; Hendrick Motorsports driver Kyle Larson (5) during NASCAR Cup Series Practice and Qualifying at Martinsville Speedway. Mandatory Credit: Greg Atkins-Imagn Images Pit by Numbers also pointed out why Larson’s championship position is not simply the result of a flawed points system. The Hendrick Motorsports driver has led 1,238 laps this season, the most in the Cup Series. Denny Hamlin has led 993. So, Larson’s four crashes and average finish do not tell the whole story of his season. When he has avoided trouble, he has spent more time running at the front than any other driver. As Pit by Numbers argued, the points reward the driver who consistently runs up front. Larson has done that more than anyone, even if his results have also included some difficult weekends. It makes the debate less straightforward. Hamlin has been remarkably consistent, but Larson has demonstrated a greater ability to lead races and accumulate the kind of results that keep him ahead in the championship standings. Kyle Larson is going to win this championship with four crashes, a 14.7 average finish, and 20 head to head losses to Denny Hamlin in 34 races. Hamlin: zero DNFs, 9.1 average finish, best in the series. Larson leads by 73 with two to go. If this were any other sport we'd call… — PitByNumbers | NASCAR Data (@pitbynumbers) November 1, 2026 NASCAR Fans Divided Over What The Championship Should Reward The discussion quickly spread on X, where fans disagreed over whether Larson’s potential title exposes a problem with the playoff format. One fan pushed back against the criticism, arguing that the top seed does not automatically win championships in other sports’ playoff systems. “It’s not broken because the #1 seed doesn’t win every year in every sports playoff system,” the fan wrote . They also argued that Hamlin had been outperformed throughout the Chase, not only by Larson but by his own teammates, adding that four crashes over a 36-race season should not automatically disqualify a driver from championship contention. item.content:encoded: USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect Kyle Larson is closing in on another NASCAR Cup Series championship, but the numbers behind his title campaign have reignited the debate over whether the playoff format truly rewards the best driver of the season. According to data shared by Pit by Numbers , Larson has recorded four crashes, a 14.7 average finish and lost 20 head-to-head battles against Denny Hamlin across 34 races. Hamlin, meanwhile, has zero DNFs and a 9.1 average finish, the best in the Cup Series. Despite that contrast, Larson holds a 73-point championship advantage with two races remaining. At first glance, it looks like a clear argument against the current format. But there is another side to the numbers. Larson’s Lap-Leading Advantage Changes the Argument Oct 31, 2026; Martinsville, Virginia, USA; Hendrick Motorsports driver Kyle Larson (5) during NASCAR Cup Series Practice and Qualifying at Martinsville Speedway. Mandatory Credit: Greg Atkins-Imagn Images Pit by Numbers also pointed out why Larson’s championship position is not simply the result of a flawed points system. The Hendrick Motorsports driver has led 1,238 laps this season, the most in the Cup Series. Denny Hamlin has led 993. So, Larson’s four crashes and average finish do not tell the whole story of his season. When he has avoided trouble, he has spent more time running at the front than any other driver. As Pit by Numbers argued, the points reward the driver who consistently runs up front. Larson has done that more than anyone, even if his results have also included some difficult weekends. It makes the debate less straightforward. Hamlin has been remarkably consistent, but Larson has demonstrated a greater ability to lead races and accumulate the kind of results that keep him ahead in the championship standings. Kyle Larson is going to win this championship with four crashes, a 14.7 average finish, and 20 head to head losses to Denny Hamlin in 34 races. Hamlin: zero DNFs, 9.1 average finish, best in the series. Larson leads by 73 with two to go. If this were any other sport we'd call… — PitByNumbers | NASCAR Data (@pitbynumbers) November 1, 2026 NASCAR Fans Divided Over What The Championship Should Reward The discussion quickly spread on X, where fans disagreed over whether Larson’s potential title exposes a problem with the playoff format. One fan pushed back against the criticism, arguing that the top seed does not automatically win championships in other sports’ playoff systems. “It’s not broken because the #1 seed doesn’t win every year in every sports playoff system,” the fan wrote . They also argued that Hamlin had been outperformed throughout the Chase, not only by Larson but by his own teammates, adding that four crashes over a 36-race season should not automatically disqualify a driver from championship contention. Another response was much less interested in comparing NASCAR with other sports. “Playoffs are for stick and ball sports, go watch them, because you aren’t race fans,” the user wrote. That reaction shows a familiar divide among NASCAR fans. Some enjoy the pressure and unpredictability of the playoff system, while others believe a season-long championship would better recognise consistency across the entire schedule. Format Raises Teams’ Strategy Question FOX Sports’ Bob Pockrass added another dimension to the discussion. He acknowledged that, based on the mathematics, Hamlin would likely be the champion under a different points calculation. However, he also warned against assuming that the standings would have unfolded in exactly the same way under a full-season championship. “I am aware of math than Hamlin would be the likely champion,” Pockrass said, while pointing out that drivers and teams would have approached races and their overall season strategies differently if they had been competing for a full-season title. A championship format does not just determine the winner, it influences how teams race. Strategy, risk-taking and decisions throughout the season are shaped by the points system in place. Is NASCAR Rewarding The Best Season or The Best Championship Campaign? Larson’s situation puts two different definitions of success against each other. The argument over NASCAR’s championship format has also turned into a debate about how other sports decide their champions. One fan pointed to some of the most dominant regular-season teams in American sports history that still failed to win the title. “In this century the 73–9 Warriors, 111 win Dodgers, and 18–1 Patriots didnt win those championships,” the fan wrote. I remember the 9-7 New York Giants taking out the undefeated New England Patriots. I guess the NFL is broken too? — Blake R. Browning (@Blycan5) November 1, 2026 The comparison was intended to challenge the idea that the best-performing team or competitor throughout the regular season must also become champion. In basketball, baseball and football, playoff results can overturn an outstanding regular season. NASCAR supporters making that argument believe racing should not be treated differently. Others pushed back, arguing that motorsports cannot simply be judged by the same standards as stick-and-ball sports. One fan brought television ratings into the discussion, questioning why NASCAR should copy formats used by the NBA and NFL when the sports have different audiences and competitive structures. The response was blunt: “There’s a reason why in motorsports they don’t crown off relevancy and who won the latest race.” The exchange captures the divide among fans. Some want NASCAR to reward season-long consistency, while others believe the playoff system creates the uncertainty and pressure that make the championship compelling. So, is NASCAR’s championship format broken? Or is it simply doing what a playoff system is designed to do: leave the title undecided until the final races, even when the regular-season numbers suggest another driver has been stronger? item.title: ‘We’ll be back’: Angel Reese sends message after losing Game 7 of WNBA Finals
item.description: Oct 31, 2026; San Francisco, California, USA; Atlanta Dream forward Angel Reese (5) after missing a free throw against the Golden State Valkyries during the fourth quarter of game seven of the 2026 WNBA Finals at Chase Center. Mandatory Credit: Kelley L Cox-Imagn Images The Atlanta Dream came up one win short of a WNBA championship on Saturday night, falling to the Golden State Valkyries in the first Game 7 in Finals history. But Angel Reese isn’t worried about the team’s future. Despite a quiet night of her own, Reese said after the game that she is proud of what the Dream accomplished this season. And she made it clear that she expects Atlanta to be right back in the mix next year. Valkyries Win First Title The Dream took a 2-1 lead in the series before dropping two straight games. They forced a Game 7 by beating the Valkyries 80-69 in Game 6 on Thursday, with Allisha Gray and Rhyne Howard combining for 44 points. Atlanta led by nine points midway through the third quarter of Game 7 at Chase Center. But Gabby Williams scored 28 of her 30 points in the second half to lead the Valkyries to a 68-63 win, earning Finals MVP honors as Golden State won its first championship in just its second season. Reese had been a force early in the series, combining for 51 points and 28 rebounds in Atlanta’s wins in Games 2 and 3. But she struggled late in the series, finishing Game 7 with eight points on 3-of-7 shooting, 12 rebounds, and four turnovers. The series also drew attention off the court. Both teams stayed off the court for the national anthem in all seven games, drawing criticism from conservatives, including President Donald Trump, but the players did what they could to keep the focus on basketball in the hotly-contested series. ‘We’ll Be Back’ After the loss, Reese said that the defeat was hard to take, but she’s confident in the team. “It is tough in the moment, but we’ll be back,” Reese said, via OutKick’s Dan Zaksheske . Reese, who won a national championship at LSU in 2023, credited her teammates for helping her grow during her first season in Atlanta. “I’m really proud of the year that I had,” Reese said. “I mean, I’ve done a lot of great things this year, but I wouldn’t be able to do it without this group.” “I’m a young player and I’m very vocal, but I think they really helped me a lot mature in different ways that I haven’t really been challenged,” she added. “And they really challenged me to be better every single day.” Reese said that the team’s chemistry is why she believes Atlanta can win a title. “There’s no egos in the locker room and nobody’s selfish,” Reese said. “Like, everybody just wants to see each other succeed.” “When you have a team like that, I’ve been a part of some teams and I know what it takes to win a championship,” she continued. “And that’s the winning mindset.” ‘Forever Grateful’ Reese also thanked Atlanta’s fans for their support throughout the season. “I love these girls. item.title: Saints finally get good injury news on Jordyn Tyson amid lengthy IR stint
item.description: Saints finally get good injury news on Jordyn Tyson amid lengthy IR stint originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The New Orleans Saints are having a rough 2026 season, and heading into their Week 8 bye, the Saints are in last place in the NFC South, tied at 2-5 with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers . While they might not be out of the divisional race just yet, the Saints really need things to turn around soon, or else this season will end in disappointment. Fortunately, during their bye week, the Saints got some great news on a key injured player. According to ESPN's Adam Schefter , Jordyn Tyson, the team's first-round rookie wide receiver who's been on injured reserve for the entire season thus far, is getting very close to returning. There's even a chance he's good to go for Week 9. Saints finally get good news on rookie WR Jordyn Tyson "Saints first-pick Jordyn Tyson could return from the hamstring injury that has sidelined him as early as next week vs. the Browns , per sources," Schefter reports. "But even if it's not then, he is not far away from playing." The Saints are getting close to seeing their first-round, No. 8 overall rookie wide receiver make his NFL debut. He suffered a hamstring injury leading up to the regular season, causing him to land on IR. He's since missed seven games, and with the Week 8 bye giving the Saints an early-season week off, it makes sense that Tyson missed those first seven weeks. MORE : NFL insiders reveal four landing spots for Colts ’ Jonathan Taylor Rushing him back before the bye would've made no sense, especially for a team that's likely still trying to climb out of the bottom of the NFC. But now, Tyson is closing in on a return to action, which would make for his NFL debut the moment he's active and steps on the field for New Orleans. Chris Olave and Devaughn Vele have been great in his absence, but getting Tyson back would be huge for the Saints this season. Even if they don't make the playoffs, seeing what Tyson can offer is still very important to the Saints. While it's too soon to tell if Tyson will be good to go for Week 9, his status will be one to monitor this upcoming week, as his chances of returning from IR are better than ever. But now, Tyson is closing in on a return to action, which would make for his NFL debut the moment he's active and steps on the field for New Orleans. Chris Olave and Devaughn Vele have been great in his absence, but getting Tyson back would be huge for the Saints this season. Even if they don't make the playoffs, seeing what Tyson can offer is still very important to the Saints. While it's too soon to tell if Tyson will be good to go for Week 9, his status will be one to monitor this upcoming week, as his chances of returning from IR are better than ever. item.title: Mets predicted to sign $32M two-time Cy Young winner to create nasty duo with Nolan McLean
item.description: Mets predicted to sign $32M two-time Cy Young winner to create nasty duo with Nolan McLean originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The New York Mets are hoping to have a much better season in 2027 after falling well short of making the playoffs in 2026. It was a disappointing campaign, to say the least, and one the organization would like to put behind it. New York is expected to make some major moves in free agency, and starting pitching could be its biggest area of need. “The Mets need starting pitching. They've needed it for several years now. In 2025, their depth evaporated down the stretch, so they missed the playoffs. In 2026, their depth imploded early, so they never recovered. To make the playoffs in 2027, they will need more of it. Exactly what they have, and therefore what they need, is in the eye of the beholder. But a few things are indisputable: Nolan McLean looks like a No. 1,” SNY’s Chelsea Janes wrote. The Mets could make a major splash this offseason, and Fox Sports believes they have a chance to sign Tarik Skubal. “The top payroll in Major League Baseball earned a last-place finish in its division. In summation: The New York Mets need a major boost, pronto, and Skubal would emphatically fill a years-long void. Skubal would become New York's undisputed ace. He offers a potent left-hander who posts strikeouts at a high rate, can pitch deep into games and does so while consistently throwing four pitches (four-seamer, changeup, sinker and slider), with a curveball mixed in every here and there,” Fox Sports wrote. The biggest concern, however, is that the two-time Cy Young Award winner reportedly enjoyed his time with the Los Angeles Dodgers this season. “The sense I get from people that he has talked to, is that he would love to be a Los Angeles Dodger. He loved his time in LA. I think it's a perfect marriage in LA," MLB insider Bowden said. The harsh reality is that there might not be an opportunity for Skubal to join the Dodgers if a rule is put in place that prevents such a move. That could leave the left-hander waiting a while before deciding where he wants to sign. Skubal played on a $32 million contract this season. If the Mets have a realistic shot at landing the left-handed ace, there is no doubt they will put all their chips on the table. Adding a pitcher of his caliber would bring some serious excitement back to the organization. item.title: Pro Bowl WR Leads Steelers Inactives vs. Browns
item.description: Pittsburgh Steelers wide receiver Ben Skowronek during a game against the Indianapolis Colts on Nov. 2, 2025. Ed Thompson / Steelers Now PITTSBURGH — Before Sunday afternoon’s rivalry matchup with the Cleveland Browns, the Pittsburgh Steelers announced their inactives, a group that includes receiver Ben Skowronek (calf). Skowronek was a limited participant in the Steelers’ Wednesday, Thursday and Friday practices. He was listed as questionable for the clash, but will have to wait another week to be reinserted in a fluid receiver room. Skowronek was selected to last year’s Pro Bowl as a special teamer. The Steelers elevated Brandon Johnson to the active roster on Saturday, the third and final time that he can be brought up from the practice squad this season. Mike McCarthy’s team is still without Michael Pittman Jr. (foot) and Roman Wilson (hand), who are still on injured reserve. Cornerbacks Brandin Echols and Doneiko Slaughter , both dealing with hamstring issues, are also out, joining rookies Drew Allar and Eli Heidenreich . As he has for every other game this season, Will Howard will serve as McCarthy’s emergency third quarterback. Heidenreich, a Mt. Lebanon product and seventh-round pick in April’s 2026 NFL Draft, has taken a backseat to Lew Nichols in the running back room. Heidenreich hasn’t played since the Steelers’ Week 2 loss on the road against the New England Patriots. Jaylen Warren has obviously been the team’s top ballcarrier, with Rico Dowdle also back in the fold. item.title: Cowboys reportedly interested in Cardinals pass rusher Josh Sweat
item.description: Like every other team, the Dallas Cowboys are looking at the trade market prior to the Nov. 10 trade deadline. The Cowboys are coming off a 38-21 win over the Philadelphia Eagles on “Monday Night Football” and are 3-4 going into Sunday’s game against the Arizona Cardinals . MORE : Will Dalton Kincaid play in Week 8? Injury update, fantasy advice for Bills TE Speaking of that game, according to ESPN’s Adam Schefter, the Cowboys are a team to watch for Cardinals’ outside linebacker Josh Sweat. They’ll get to see him in person on Sunday. There is interest in Cardinals OLB Josh Sweat, per sources. A team to watch with Sweat is the Cowboys, who will get an up close look at him today, when Dallas hosts Arizona. pic.twitter.com/mNa42KxN1z — Adam Schefter (@AdamSchefter) November 1, 2026 How has Josh Sweat played this season? Arizona Cardinals linebacker Josh Sweat (10) chases after Denver Broncos quarterback Bo Nix (10) at State Farm Stadium in Glendale on Oct. 25, 2026. Credit: USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Sweat is in his second season with the Cardinals and has played in seven games this year, compiling 16 tackles and two sacks. He finished the 2025 season with 30 total tackles, 12 sacks, four forced fumbles, a fumble recovery, and two passes defended. Prior to these last two seasons, Sweat spent seven seasons with the Eagles and was one of their better pass rushers. He has 57 career sacks in 128 games. The Cowboys’ defense has struggled to start the season, so it makes sense they’d want Sweat to help rush the passer. Kickoff for Sunday’s Cowboys-Cardinals game will be at 1 p.m. ET on FOX. Joe Davis and Greg Olsen will have the call. — Enjoy free coverage of the top news & trending stories with The Big Lead Newsletter —

item.title: "You Can Get Fired"- Connor Zilisch Reveals Shocking Stakes Behind Iconic Sponsor’s ‘Athlete-Only’ Status Symbol
item.description: ©IMAGO/Icon Sportswire Connor Zilisch has spent the last two years collecting things most drivers his age only dream about: a place in Red Bull’s athlete family, a full-time Cup Series ride at Trackhouse Racing and, since August, a future seat in Hendrick Motorsports’ No. 48. Yet one perk of that world, he says, cannot be bought at any price. The rule attached to it is far stricter than most fans would ever guess. “So yeah, if you try to go buy one of these, you can’t. If you are an athlete and you give a hat to somebody and you get caught, you can get fired,” t he Trackhouse driver explained in an interview with PRN on ‘Garage Pass’. When asked whether Red Bull gives its athletes exclusive hats, Zilisch explained the distinction between merchandise available to fans and the gear reserved for those representing the brand. “Yeah, any hat you see with the Red Bull logo on it is only for athletes,” he explained. “You can’t buy a Red Bull hat with just the Red Bull logo. You can buy hats with the Trackhouse logo or the Red Bull Racing logo. So anything with just the actual Red Bull logo is only for athletes.” The pressure behind NASCAR's most exclusive badge just got real. Subscribe to stay updated on the stakes shaping the sport's next generation. The company has been known to be strict about their branding, and cases where this is given away can lead to it being considered a breach of contract. “It’s pretty cool,” he continued. “Whenever you are at an event or if you’re out and about and you see someone with a hat, unless they’ve bought a knockoff one off eBay or something, most of the time, they’re, you know, a professional athlete and, you know, you can relate and walk up to them, and they’re going to know that, you know, we’re in a club of, you know, only a couple hundred athletes.” The restriction turns a baseball cap into something closer to a membership card. In a sport where fans routinely buy replica hats and team gear, the standalone Red Bull logo works differently. It marks the wearer as part of the company’s athlete roster, not just someone cheering for its racing teams. For Connor Zilisch, though, the appeal goes beyond owning something supporters cannot purchase. His explanation centers on recognition. Red Bull’s roster spans very different sports, and the hat gives athletes a quick way to spot one another and start a conversation with someone who understands the pressure of competing professionally. By his own estimate, the group numbers only a couple hundred people, which is what makes a chance meeting feel special. item.content:encoded: ©IMAGO/Icon Sportswire Connor Zilisch has spent the last two years collecting things most drivers his age only dream about: a place in Red Bull’s athlete family, a full-time Cup Series ride at Trackhouse Racing and, since August, a future seat in Hendrick Motorsports’ No. 48. Yet one perk of that world, he says, cannot be bought at any price. The rule attached to it is far stricter than most fans would ever guess. “So yeah, if you try to go buy one of these, you can’t. If you are an athlete and you give a hat to somebody and you get caught, you can get fired,” t he Trackhouse driver explained in an interview with PRN on ‘Garage Pass’. When asked whether Red Bull gives its athletes exclusive hats, Zilisch explained the distinction between merchandise available to fans and the gear reserved for those representing the brand. “Yeah, any hat you see with the Red Bull logo on it is only for athletes,” he explained. “You can’t buy a Red Bull hat with just the Red Bull logo. You can buy hats with the Trackhouse logo or the Red Bull Racing logo. So anything with just the actual Red Bull logo is only for athletes.” The pressure behind NASCAR's most exclusive badge just got real. Subscribe to stay updated on the stakes shaping the sport's next generation. The company has been known to be strict about their branding, and cases where this is given away can lead to it being considered a breach of contract. “It’s pretty cool,” he continued. “Whenever you are at an event or if you’re out and about and you see someone with a hat, unless they’ve bought a knockoff one off eBay or something, most of the time, they’re, you know, a professional athlete and, you know, you can relate and walk up to them, and they’re going to know that, you know, we’re in a club of, you know, only a couple hundred athletes.” The restriction turns a baseball cap into something closer to a membership card. In a sport where fans routinely buy replica hats and team gear, the standalone Red Bull logo works differently. It marks the wearer as part of the company’s athlete roster, not just someone cheering for its racing teams. For Connor Zilisch, though, the appeal goes beyond owning something supporters cannot purchase. His explanation centers on recognition. Red Bull’s roster spans very different sports, and the hat gives athletes a quick way to spot one another and start a conversation with someone who understands the pressure of competing professionally. By his own estimate, the group numbers only a couple hundred people, which is what makes a chance meeting feel special. That sense of belonging stands out in motorsports, where sponsorship is usually visible through paint schemes, firesuits, and appearances. A partnership can put a company’s colors on the car and connect a driver with fans. Red Bull’s athlete community adds something else: a NASCAR driver can find common ground with a Formula 1 racer, or with an athlete from a completely different sport, simply because they belong to the same program. Red Bull’s NASCAR return gives Connor Zilisch a wider platform The hat comes with a long history behind it. Red Bull fielded its own Cup Series team from 2007 through 2011 before leaving the sport. The brand returned in January 2025, when Trackhouse announced Red Bull as the team’s official energy drink. Zilisch and Shane van Gisbergen were already Red Bull athletes by then, van Gisbergen since 2016 and Zilisch since 2024. Zilisch has said he was surprised when Red Bull presented him with his helmet and hat that year. The 2025 deal put Red Bull colors on van Gisbergen’s car for five Cup races and on Zilisch’s Cup debut at Circuit of the Americas. For 2026, Red Bull expanded its role, splitting 25 primary sponsorship races between Zilisch’s No. 88 and van Gisbergen’s No. 97. The timing matters for Zilisch. He won 11 O’Reilly Series races for JR Motorsports last season, then moved up to Trackhouse for his rookie Cup campaign. In August, Hendrick Motorsports announced a multi-year deal that will put him in the No. 48 Chevrolet, replacing Alex Bowman, beginning in 2028. Zilisch is set to remain in Trackhouse’s No. 88 through 2027. There is also a practical side to being around experienced athletes. Scott Speed, a former Formula 1 driver who raced for Red Bull’s own Cup team from 2008 to 2010, has been part of Zilisch’s development since 2022, helping with simulator work and advice. Speed and van Gisbergen were also the ones who surprised Zilisch with his Red Bull-designed helmet at Watkins Glen in 2024. That mix of stock car and Red Bull experience gives the young driver a perspective few of his peers can match. The conversation eventually returned to Zilisch’s own headwear when the interviewer pointed out that his hat carried the Trackhouse logo. “It’s got the Trackhouse logo.” “I know. Yeah, this one’s custom. If you get caught, like, that must have been Shane’s. Yeah, exactly. I’ll always blame it on Shane.” The joke offered a lighter ending to an otherwise revealing exchange. To fans, a Red Bull hat might look like any other piece of sponsor merchandise. To Zilisch, it represents access to a much smaller community, one that connects athletes across disciplines and opens doors beyond the racetrack. The logo is familiar, but the privilege attached to wearing it is anything but ordinary. item.title: Jamie Carragher warns Ryan Gravenberch may never recover after Andoni Iraola picks teenager Trey Nyoni against Arsenal
item.description: Liverpool v Manchester City - Premier League 2026/27 - Getty Images Sport Jamie Carragher fears Ryan Gravenberch may never recover from being dropped for 19-year-old Trey Nyoni, who makes his first Premier League start against Arsenal at Anfield on Sunday. Andoni Iraola has left the Netherlands international on the bench for the crunch clash, a decision Carragher believes will be "a mighty blow" for the experienced midfielder. Nyoni handed first Premier League start against Arsenal Iraola has made a bold call by handing Nyoni his first Premier League start in Sunday's huge clash, with Gravenberch left among the substitutes. The teenager has already made 20 appearances for Liverpool, 14 of them this season, and has started in the Champions League. Gravenberch had returned for the win over Brighton after a one-game ban for his red card against Manchester City, and started alongside Nyoni in Wednesday's Carabao Cup win over Chelsea on penalties after a 1-1 draw. Alexis Mac Allister partners the youngster behind Florian Wirtz, while Dominik Szoboszlai is on the bench after injury. Carragher: It's always difficult for the senior player to recover Speaking on Sky Sports, Carragher said: "The one thing that has stood out with the manager so far is he's not afraid to make big decisions. He dropped Gravenberch really early, after the first game of the season, away at Newcastle. He's left [Milos] Kerkez out, a player who he knows before as well. He's changed the wingers in and out at different times. "What I would say is, I think we all go back to being a young player; the first time as a youngster when you're ever picked ahead of what you [think] is an established player. It's always difficult, I think, for the senior player to ever recover from that. Not that he can't come back, but Iraola's saying he's got more trust in a 19-year-old kid who's only getting better and his career is going one way. I think that will be a mighty blow for Gravenberch." Recalling his own breakthrough, he added: "I always remember it was Michael Thomas, central midfield, the manager Roy Evans putting me in." Iraola trusts Nyoni '100 per cent' as Sturridge backs the call Explaining his selection to Sky Sports, Iraola said: "It's not about me, it's about Trey. He has shown that he has the level. He has been very good on the ball for us, very good without the ball. He understands the game. Obviously it's a big challenge for him, but we trust him 100 per cent. He covers a lot of space and he's aggressive without the ball, he's calm in possession and he's good in communicating with his team-mates." Former Liverpool striker Daniel Sturridge agreed with the decision. He said: "I like it. I like it, man. I think Trey has been really good so far this season. Looks so comfortable in possession. Not shy to drop in between the defence. Picks passes in between the lines. He's intercepting passes as well at a high clip. Gravenberch hasn't been at his best. We know he's a top player, one who

item.title: No. 11 Texas 31, Mississippi State 3: Five observations and Sunday chat
item.description: AUSTIN, TX - OCTOBER 31: Texas Longhorns linebacker Rasheem Biles #3 sacks Mississippi State Bulldogs quarterback AJ Swann #17 that results in a fumble and touchdown during the SEC football game between the Texas Longhorns and Mississippi State Bulldogs on October 31, 2026, at Darrell K Royal-Texas Memorial Stadium in Austin, TX. (Photo by David Buono/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Nightmare on the Forty Acres🤘 pic.twitter.com/vrksH42dmV — Texas Football (@TexasFootball) November 1, 2026 And just like that, the No. 11 Texas Longhorns completed the sweep of the state of Mississippi. The Mississippi State Bulldogs came into this matchup wounded and already down their star quarterback Kamario Taylor, then they lost their RB1 in Fluff Bothwell in the second half. It’s been a rough go for Jeff Lebby’s squad after starting the season 4-0. They have now dropped four games in a row and still have three SEC games left to play. They will need to win one of those if they want to go bowling, and from the looks of things they will be down to QB3 after AJ Swann hurt his shoulder last night. On the Longhorns’ side of the ledger, they took care of business and covered a pretty big spread, which has been tough for them to do in recent memory. A win and a cover is always good for the home team and you will take them however you can get them. However, there are still plenty of nits to pick within the context of the game and we will get into that now. The offense turned in a sub-par performance Let’s get the positive out of the way. Arch Manning was 16-of-20 passing for 220 yards and three touchdowns, which is pretty effective, all things considered. The opening drive of the game consisted of a throw into tight coverage to Cam Coleman that went for an explosive play and was quickly followed up by another nice throw to Coleman for a touchdown to kick off the scoring. item.content:encoded: AUSTIN, TX - OCTOBER 31: Texas Longhorns linebacker Rasheem Biles #3 sacks Mississippi State Bulldogs quarterback AJ Swann #17 that results in a fumble and touchdown during the SEC football game between the Texas Longhorns and Mississippi State Bulldogs on October 31, 2026, at Darrell K Royal-Texas Memorial Stadium in Austin, TX. (Photo by David Buono/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Nightmare on the Forty Acres🤘 pic.twitter.com/vrksH42dmV — Texas Football (@TexasFootball) November 1, 2026 And just like that, the No. 11 Texas Longhorns completed the sweep of the state of Mississippi. The Mississippi State Bulldogs came into this matchup wounded and already down their star quarterback Kamario Taylor, then they lost their RB1 in Fluff Bothwell in the second half. It’s been a rough go for Jeff Lebby’s squad after starting the season 4-0. They have now dropped four games in a row and still have three SEC games left to play. They will need to win one of those if they want to go bowling, and from the looks of things they will be down to QB3 after AJ Swann hurt his shoulder last night. On the Longhorns’ side of the ledger, they took care of business and covered a pretty big spread, which has been tough for them to do in recent memory. A win and a cover is always good for the home team and you will take them however you can get them. However, there are still plenty of nits to pick within the context of the game and we will get into that now. The offense turned in a sub-par performance Let’s get the positive out of the way. Arch Manning was 16-of-20 passing for 220 yards and three touchdowns, which is pretty effective, all things considered. The opening drive of the game consisted of a throw into tight coverage to Cam Coleman that went for an explosive play and was quickly followed up by another nice throw to Coleman for a touchdown to kick off the scoring. CAM WITH AN EARLY THRILLER🤘 pic.twitter.com/4cDklc3agP — Texas Football (@TexasFootball) October 31, 2026 Manning followed that up with a couple more touchdown tosses on the evening, including one to Emmett Mosley V where he broke free of the coverage and was streaking down the field for an easy score on third and short. DROPPED A DOT🤘 pic.twitter.com/N1TzmDS1kQ — Texas Football (@TexasFootball) November 1, 2026 Now let’s get to the not-so-great aspects of the offense, and that includes Manning himself. Manning had another turnover that was a byproduct of him holding the ball way too long in the pocket instead of either checking it down, running, or throwing it away. A disastrous play from Arch Manning coughs the ball up to Mississippi State. pic.twitter.com/NP86Ts09OY — Underdog CFB (@UnderdogCFB) November 1, 2026 This is the type of sack that is not on the offensive line whatsoever. Not all sacks are created equal, and this is a play that didn’t need to happen. Manning has a clear check-down opportunity to Raleek Brown at the top of the screen and waits far too long before deciding to take that option. The indecisiveness and the internal clock for Manning has been an issue all year long. On top of that turnover, Manning has to do a better job of protecting himself when he does decide to take off and run. Everyone can recall when he took a huge hit earlier in the year where his helmet popped off. Well, that happened again on Saturday against Mississippi State. Arch Manning just got ABSOLUTELY SMOKED 😭 pic.twitter.com/p7qbHtZM3Y — Daily Stinkers (@DailyStinkers) November 1, 2026 I am a fan of Arch using his wheels more to help move the offense down the field, but I am also a fan of him protecting himself when he opts to do so. He can’t keep taking hits like this and has to protect himself better if he wants to make it through the entire season. Also on the negative side of the ledger, the Texas run game was horrific — 60 rushing yards on 32 carries for a whopping 1.8 yards per carry. A week after your best rushing performance of the year, the Texas offense turns in what is likely to be its worst. This falls on everyone in the offensive ecosystem, and the inconsistency continues to be maddening. The 280 yards of total offense is not going to get it done against better opponents. Hell, it probably would not have got it done against Mississippi State had Kamario Taylor been healthy. The Texas defense continues to be elite BIG MAN TOUCHDOWN FOR MARAAD WATSON🤘 pic.twitter.com/kiqiDlfxu8 — Texas Football (@TexasFootball) November 1, 2026 Someone, please edit this play to have Chris Berman narrating Maraad Watson’s THICC-SIX from Saturday. The big fella was rumbling and stumbling all the way to the end zone, and I know he needed the oxygen tank after this play. The Texas defense continues to play at a very high level. With Taylor out of the lineup, Will Muschamp made life hard regardless of who was under center for Jeff Lebby and the Bulldogs. The defense held the State offense to under 200 yards of total offense, only surrendered three points, and only allowed six conversions on 19 attempts on money downs. The Texas defense tallied seven sacks and inflicted nine additional tackles for a loss on the night and this was all with Colin Simmons on the sideline. Just a fantastic job by this group all around. If you want to pick nits, they did have a hard time tackling Bothwell during the game, but Bothwell ultimately was held in check and never got loose before going out with an injury of his own. Rasheem Biles has been worth every penny Number three in burnt orange has been gangbusters this year, man. Texas LB Rasheem Biles is the old quote “got a football magnet in his helmet” In 8 games for Texas: 🐂61 tkls, 4 sacks, 3 FF, 3 INT Last year at Pitt: 🔹100 tkls, 4.5 sacks, 2 FF, 2 INT pic.twitter.com/jO5ku8HcAP — Clint Goss (@NFLDraftDome) November 1, 2026 Biles was everywhere on Saturday for Texas once again. Biles tallied a career-high three sacks, forced two fumbles (including the one returned for a touchdown), and had an additional four tackles for a loss. Just an absolute stat sheet filler. Muschamp has unleashed him in a variety of ways on opposing offenses, and he has been incredibly tough to deal with. I will be stunned if he isn’t All-SEC come December with how well he is playing for the Longhorns right now. Texas got banged up again in this one Steve Sarkisian mentioned it after the game, but multiple players for Texas didn’t finish the game after multiple guys didn’t finish last week’s game against Ole Miss. Texas football coach Steve Sarkisian's injury update: "Graceson Littleton didn't finish the game. Cam Coleman didn't finish the game. Kade Phillips didn't finish the game. Hollywood Smothers didn't finish the game. Ryan Wingo didn't finish the game. So, all integral parts of the… pic.twitter.com/DGP6Gdyxe1 — Anwar Richardson (@AnwarRichardson) November 1, 2026 The longer these seasons get, the more imperative it becomes to try to keep guys healthy and make sure you have quality depth across the roster. Texas doesn’t have any easy outs on the remainder of the schedule, and they will likely need to win them all if they want to be in the playoff. Though, you can probably make a case for a 9-3 Texas with how this CFB season is playing out. Regardless, Texas is going to need all of the guys Sark mentioned healthy for the home stretch of the season. Coleman going back out after leaving early last week is certainly something to watch. Ditto on Smothers, since he was previously hurt and held out. Ryan Niblett got deprived of a touchdown Ryan Niblett PR TD gets called back pic.twitter.com/eEHZokkD7S — T.J. Randall (@TJ_Randall12) November 1, 2026 It should be illegal to run that far for a touchdown and it not count. But that is the Texas special teams in 2026. It is either plays like this getting called back or Niblett will have four to five guys unblocked running at him. It’s a shame Texas is not going to be able to maximize his ability as a

item.title: Fox put together rare performance in Spurs' victory over Timberwolves
item.description: San Antonio Spurs guard De'Aaron Fox (4) drives against Minnesota Timberwolves forward Jonathan Kuminga (24) at the Frost Bank Center in San Antonio, Texas on Saturday, Oct. 31, 2026. The San Antonio Spurs defeated the Minnesota Timberwolves 121-111. (Katina Zentz/San Antonio Express-News) Spurs All-Star guard De'Aaron Fox accomplished something in Saturday's 121-111 victory over Minnesota that has rarely happened in franchise history. Fox finished with 22 points on 8-of-10 shooting from the field, a team-high eight rebounds (including two on the offensive end) and a team-best seven assists in 35 minutes, marking just the fifth game in which a Spur has had 20-plus points, eight-plus rebounds and seven-plus assists while shooting 80% from the floor. Jakob Poeltl (2022), Gene Banks (1983, 1985) and Billy Paultz (1978) are the other players to do it. "Just trying to be efficient, trying to affect the game in different ways, get downhill," said Fox, who notched his first 20-point game of the season in helping the Spurs win their fourth in a row to improve to 4-2. Through six games, Fox is averaging 16.5 points on 57.6% shooting, 4.8 rebounds, a team-high 7.0 assists and 1.5 steals. "We know to go to him," said All-Star center Victor Wembanyama, who led the Spurs with 43 points. "We know to put the ball in his hands. He knows to go get the ball. And he's been reacting defensively too. So, it's a true point guard." Subscribe There’s more to San Antonio with the Express-News. Subscribe today for just 25¢. item.title: In a city under attack, Canelo Alvarez became the definition of calm under fire
item.description: The reason why Mexican boxers tend to be so revered has a lot to do with their willingness to put themselves in harm’s way. Consult the archives and you will discover they all did it: Chavez, Sanchez, Lopez, Marquez, Olivares, Saldivar, Zarate, Barrera, Morales and so on. Not only did each of these men put themselves in harm’s way, they did so with a rare grace and intelligence, almost as if it was part of the strategy; something they had, in the 14-foot-by-14-foot rings in Mexico, over time learned to master. To any great Mexican fighter, the idea of being in harm’s way means opportunity. More than just an act of bravado, it increases the likelihood of an opponent opening up, getting careless, and offering a target to hit. It also means action, excitement, admiration. If in doubt, just listen to the crowd on fight night. Seemingly, the more these men put themselves in harm’s way, the louder the arena becomes and the more people are inclined to watch. Sometimes, with such a price placed on machismo , putting themselves in harm’s way can feel like the only way for these warriors. With all that said, few Mexican boxers have ever put themselves in harm’s way quite like Saul “Canelo” Alvarez did this weekend in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia . If it wasn’t enough to face and defuse the attacks of Christian Mbilli, the WBC super middleweight champion, the fighter from Guadalajara had to also contend with the pervasive threat of attacks from Iranian-supported Houthi rebels , which have so far claimed the lives of at least 20 people and injured at least 370 in Riyadh. As well it might, this put a very different spin on the idea of a Mexican boxer finding themselves in harm’s way. No matter the talent or courage, to come through the ordeal and return home in one piece would require more than just an ability to fight inside, a granite chin, and short punches. It would also require nerve, perhaps even an ignorance. Most of all, it would require an element of good fortune on the part of Alvarez and all who traveled. For Saúl "Canelo" Álvarez, the show must go on. Mark Robinson via Getty Images Indeed, just 48 hours before the first bell, everybody in Riyadh had been warned via an emergency alert sent to mobile phones to be vigilant and prepared. According to those on the ground, the message received was as follows: “Warning. City of Riyadh is under a hostile aerial threat. Please remain calm, stay indoors or in a safe place away from windows and doors, and follow the instructions of Civil Defense.” This was then accompanied by a social media post from Turki Alalshikh, the man responsible for bringing Mbilli vs. Alvarez to Riyadh, which said, quite simply: “May God protect Riyadh and all who are in it.” Of course, the biggest challenge for Alvarez and Mbilli would have been maintaining focus and concentration, both throughout fight week and on the night itself. item.dc:creator: Elliot Worsell
item.content:encoded: The reason why Mexican boxers tend to be so revered has a lot to do with their willingness to put themselves in harm’s way. Consult the archives and you will discover they all did it: Chavez, Sanchez, Lopez, Marquez, Olivares, Saldivar, Zarate, Barrera, Morales and so on. Not only did each of these men put themselves in harm’s way, they did so with a rare grace and intelligence, almost as if it was part of the strategy; something they had, in the 14-foot-by-14-foot rings in Mexico, over time learned to master. To any great Mexican fighter, the idea of being in harm’s way means opportunity. More than just an act of bravado, it increases the likelihood of an opponent opening up, getting careless, and offering a target to hit. It also means action, excitement, admiration. If in doubt, just listen to the crowd on fight night. Seemingly, the more these men put themselves in harm’s way, the louder the arena becomes and the more people are inclined to watch. Sometimes, with such a price placed on machismo , putting themselves in harm’s way can feel like the only way for these warriors. With all that said, few Mexican boxers have ever put themselves in harm’s way quite like Saul “Canelo” Alvarez did this weekend in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia . If it wasn’t enough to face and defuse the attacks of Christian Mbilli, the WBC super middleweight champion, the fighter from Guadalajara had to also contend with the pervasive threat of attacks from Iranian-supported Houthi rebels , which have so far claimed the lives of at least 20 people and injured at least 370 in Riyadh. As well it might, this put a very different spin on the idea of a Mexican boxer finding themselves in harm’s way. No matter the talent or courage, to come through the ordeal and return home in one piece would require more than just an ability to fight inside, a granite chin, and short punches. It would also require nerve, perhaps even an ignorance. Most of all, it would require an element of good fortune on the part of Alvarez and all who traveled. For Saúl "Canelo" Álvarez, the show must go on. Mark Robinson via Getty Images Indeed, just 48 hours before the first bell, everybody in Riyadh had been warned via an emergency alert sent to mobile phones to be vigilant and prepared. According to those on the ground, the message received was as follows: “Warning. City of Riyadh is under a hostile aerial threat. Please remain calm, stay indoors or in a safe place away from windows and doors, and follow the instructions of Civil Defense.” This was then accompanied by a social media post from Turki Alalshikh, the man responsible for bringing Mbilli vs. Alvarez to Riyadh, which said, quite simply: “May God protect Riyadh and all who are in it.” Of course, the biggest challenge for Alvarez and Mbilli would have been maintaining focus and concentration, both throughout fight week and on the night itself. Perhaps, in the end, the immediate danger in front of them was sufficient to override greater dangers, but still, for both, it must have been tough. For all the distraction offered by the incoming fists of an opponent, even the most emotionally detached boxer would struggle to shake from their mind the volatility of the situation outside the ring. Then again, boxing is nothing if not a microcosm of life in a “warzone.” In fact, every time two boxers enter a ring and throw punches with the aim to cause damage, there is an ever-present, unavoidable risk of death . They know it, we know it, yet still the show goes on; still they get in the ring and fight. They do so because, by then, they will have managed to convince themselves that death and serious injury are things that happen to other people. They do so because it is their job, all they know. Ordinarily, the more a boxer fights, the more comfortable they start to feel, both in the ring and in terms of that belief. With a boxer like Alvarez, for example, there can be no man better equipped to handle business at a time of peril and uncertainty. One look at his career, which now spans 69 professional fights, and you will find a fighter who has frequently and with relish put himself in harm’s way at every turn. From turning pro as a child at the age of 15 to boxing Floyd Mayweather at 23 and then later rising to light heavyweight to fight the likes of Sergey Kovalev and Dmitry Bivol, Alvarez has shown time and time again an ability to find comfort in situations lesser men would avoid. Even last night’s fight against Mbilli, which saw Alvarez in the position of challenger, was one many experts considered a risk . Mbilli, they said, was a potential problem for Alvarez, stylistically, what with his physical strength, his high output, and his capacity to march forward undeterred. If, as assumed, Alvarez was indeed past his best, or no longer capable of fighting with the intensity of old, the last thing he needed at this point in his career was a hungry champion like Christian Mbilli. Christian Mbilli was unable to withstand the pressure and presence of "Canelo" Alvarez. FAYEZ NURELDINE via Getty Images There were signs of this, too, during the early stages of their fight on Saturday. The opening two rounds, for instance, were rounds in which Mbilli seemed happy to be on the front foot letting his hands go with confidence. Until he was told not to, or was stung by something coming back, the Cameroonian-Frenchman had no issue forcing the pace, aware that Alvarez, for all his brilliance, had not stopped an opponent since 2021. That fact alone gave Mbilli hope, or at least the fuel to keep pushing forward and punching. When he did, it was easy to see why some had backed him to win. This was especially the case whenever he threw punches in bunches, starting them low to the body before bringing them up to the head. In such moments Mbilli provided the image judges traditionally like to see on fight night: An aggressive boxer coming forward and outworking his opponent against the ropes. It wasn’t only the judges, mind you. There was a sense as well that “Canelo” rather liked the image — that is, the feeling — of Mbilli fighting in this manner, all huff and puff. Before long, it became quite apparent he was able to read the telegraphed attacks of the champion and that, rather than being bothered by them, he was instead wanting to invite more and more of them. This led to Alvarez retreating to the ropes of his own volition and, in Round 3, beating his chest, shaking his head, and demanding Mbilli come toward him and keep throwing. He knew by now, having got the measure of Mbilli in the opening two rounds, how to tame the man in front of him. To do so, he had to put himself in harm’s way. Otherwise, it might have been difficult to penetrate Mbilli’s guard, so long were his forearms. “Canelo” tried, and had success with right hooks around the side, but clearly his preference was to have Mbilli open up first and then fire, typically with jabs and some wonderfully-picked right uppercuts. It was, of course, a high-risk strategy, as it always is when putting oneself in harm’s way, but Alvarez is a fighter experienced enough to have mastered the art of fine margins. How comfortable he looked, too, up against the ropes, beckoning Mbilli toward him. There, despite the threat, he appeared not only composed but safe. He read the trajectory of every imminent attack and often, particularly as the fight progressed, had a counter for Mbilli from a defensive position. In fact, the mere threat of a response was what ultimately reduced the number of attacks coming from Mbilli. He had, by Rounds 5 and 6, received enough spiteful shots inside, following punches of his own, to become that bit more wary of initiating exchanges and getting too carried away on the front foot. Soon he had found himself completely nullified by virtue of Alvarez’s ability to predict his every move and his own inability to produce anything different. This was never more evident than in Round 7, when Alvarez wa

item.title: Alcaraz wins Vienna Open to maintain perfect record
item.description: Carlos Alcaraz is a seven-time Grand Slam winner [Getty Images] Carlos Alcaraz powered to a straight-set win over Alex de Minaur to win the Vienna Open and maintain his perfect record in ATP 500 events this year. The Spanish second seed triumphed 6-1 6-4 in 87 minutes for his 16th straight win at that level in 2026. Alcaraz has won 26 straight matches at ATP 500 events - a run that goes back to the 2025 Barcelona Open, where he lost to Holger Rune. The 23-year-old's run this year includes titles in Doha and Tokyo. "I tried to be aggressive and show him that if he wants to win, he has to play better, more aggressive, more solid, and be smarter than me," said Alcaraz. "I'm just really happy that at the end I found my way, played great, and obviously it has been a really emotional and amazing week for me." Alcaraz started the match strongly, with his groundstrokes causing De Minaur problems. De Minaur took five of the seven games in the first set to deuce, but it was Alcaraz's quality at key moments that made the difference as he secured three breaks of serve. Alcaraz continued to apply pressure in the second set, and while De Minaur's trademark defence helped the 27-year-old Australian save three break points, he could not fend off championship point. After a gripping rally, Alcaraz whipped a forehand winner across court to seal victory, before raising both arms in celebration. The win was Alcaraz's seventh against De Minaur, maintaining his perfect head-to-head record. item.title: How Dart revived career with help of Wimbledon champion
item.description: In the hour following her first WTA title win, Britain's Harriet Dart had little time to respond to the stream of congratulatory messages flashing up on her phone. Most pressing was making a call to her proud parents, Nick and Susie, who had been watching the final with friends at their local tennis club in north London, and her sister Phoebe. The next person she spoke to was 2013 Wimbledon champion Marion Bartoli. Dart has been coached by the French former world number seven since the start of the season on a part-time basis, and she credits Bartoli for helping her achieve what some thought was beyond her. On Sunday, with Bartoli watching from home, the world number 115 won the Guangzhou Open in China by beating rising Austrian teenager Lilli Tagger. "It's been quite incredible to work with Marion, and I was really fortunate she was open to working with me," Dart, 30, told BBC Sport in a video call from Guangzhou. "I'm obviously at a very different stage of my career to someone who is, say, 20. But I still feel I have a lot to improve and there are gains to be made. "She really believes in me - that means the world to me. Seeing a Grand Slam champion having that belief has made me believe a lot more in myself." Britain's Dart wins first WTA title in 'wild week' When Dart started working with Bartoli, she was ranked outside the top 160. The pair live close to each other in Dubai and spend training blocks together there when Dart is not on the road. Dart and Bartoli, who has a young family, are not travelling full-time together on tour, but there have been opportunities for them to work on the ground, particularly during this year's Grand Slam tournaments. Dart says 42-year-old Bartoli still hitting the ball "really well" in practice is another benefit of the partnership. In Guangzhou, Dart was accompanied by her fitness trainer Dario Gonfiantini and boyfriend Stephen Falck. Without her coach, Dart had to largely rely on figuring things out herself - with the help of Bartoli sending over observational notes. Dart is projected to rise to 83rd on Monday after lifting the Guangzhou trophy to cap a stunning second half of the season. Dart has won 19 of her 24 tour-level matches on the hard courts since Wimbledon, taking her overall record on the WTA Tour this season to 23 victories from 34 matches - the highest winning percentage of her career. "More than anything, Marion is just a great person. She cares about me as a person first and foremost, as well as improving me as a tennis player, of course," Dart said. "It's been invaluable and amazing for her to share her experiences to make me better. "I've learned a lot from her and look forward to continuing to learn more. I hope we will be able to spend more weeks together next year." Bartoli, 42, has coached several WTA players since retiring, including 2017 French Open champion Jelena Ostapenko [Getty Images] Dart reached a career high of 70th in the world in 2024, having made the Wimbledon third round

"It's been invaluable and amazing for her to share her experiences to make me better. "I've learned a lot from her and look forward to continuing to learn more. I hope we will be able to spend more weeks together next year." Bartoli, 42, has coached several WTA players since retiring, including 2017 French Open champion Jelena Ostapenko [Getty Images] Dart reached a career high of 70th in the world in 2024, having made the Wimbledon third round and US Open second round, but has languished outside the top 100 for most of the past two seasons. During this period there have been clear vulnerabilities with her game, with opponents learning they could take advantage of a slow second serve that tended to produce double faults. There have also been questions about her on-court mentality and whether she could handle the pressure moments. In Guangzhou, she answered those doubts with a series of gutsy wins where she needed to fight back from behind. "She's always had a fantastic work ethic and has always set the bar high with her professionalism," Anne Keothavong, Britain's women's team captain, told BBC Sport. "But there is certainly more belief and confidence now. She's in a very good place. "She's been grinding away on the tour for a long time and it's great to see someone who has put in a lot of time to succeed and win a big title." Keothavong named Dart in her squad for September's Billie Jean King Cup Finals and although she did not select Dart to play in the tie, she was impressed by her ball-striking during practice. Taking that level back on tour has helped Dart continue what has been an encouraging few weeks for British women in the Asian hard-court swing. Sonay Kartal reached the final of a WTA 1000 event in Wuhan, Katie Boulter made the semi-finals at a WTA 250 in Osaka and now Dart has won her maiden title at WTA 250 level. Last week, teenager Hannah Klugman won the biggest title of her career at the Wrexham Open - a W100 event on the second-tier Challenger tour. "The way they're all performing towards the end of the season - at whatever level - has been impressive," added Keothavong. "It's not easy at this time of the season because there has been a lot of tennis played, but they've all capitalised and risen to the occasion. "It's great reward for all their hard work and is encouraging for British tennis." Live scores, results and order of play Get tennis news sent straight to your phone

item.title: ‘100% Deserves It,’ ‘Earned It’ – WNBA Fans React as Cathy Engelbert Is Booed During Valkyries’ Championship Ceremony
item.description: '100% Deserves It,' 'She Earned It' — WNBA Fans React as Cathy Engelbert Is Booed During Valkyries' Championship Ceremony The Golden State Valkyries won the WNBA championship on Saturday night. They beat the Atlanta Dream 68-63 at Chase Center in the first Game 7 in Finals history. During the trophy ceremony that followed, the home crowd booed WNBA commissioner Cathy Engelbert as she spoke. Fans online were quick to react as clips of the moment spread. One of them answered with a three-word verdict that sided with the crowd. Boos Greet Cathy Engelbert at the Championship Ceremony Time expired with players racing across the court and confetti raining down from above, and the sold-out crowd erupted in delirium. The jeers did not arrive until later, when Engelbert spoke to the fans at the last WNBA Finals before her retirement at the end of 2026. Game 7 fell on Halloween, and the arena known as Ballhalla had become Boohalla for the night. Gabby Williams scored 30 points and took home the MVP trophy as the Valkyries won a title in only their second season. Valkyries co-owner Joe Lacob used the same ceremony to holler “Ballhalla!” and thank a fan base that has made every Valkyries game at Chase Center a sellout since the franchise began. Another fan posted a clip of the same moment that played on the night’s Boohalla name. One fan’s clip turned the attention to Valkyries forward Janelle Salaün, who did not play in Game 7. Another fan wrote later Saturday night: “Also the WNBA fans make sure Cathy Engelbert knows how they feel about her!” Saturday was not the first time Engelbert heard it from a WNBA crowd. At the 2025 All-Star Game in Indianapolis, fans chanted “pay them” as she tried to deliver her postgame speech. She was heckled again during the trophy ceremony at the 2025 Finals. Earlier this season, at the 2026 Commissioner’s Cup championship at Barclays Center, her voice was almost entirely drowned out when she took the microphone after New York beat Las Vegas. The reaction carried into Sunday. One fan, posting that morning, went further: “She 100% deserves it. READ MORE: ‘At Least Have the Guts To Explain Why’ – Ex-Indiana Coach Calls Out Dream, Valkyries Players Skipping the National Anthem One fan replied under one of the clips: “She earned it.” The clip that fan answered had been shared minutes earlier by another fan. Another fan posted a clip of the same moment that played on the night’s Boohalla name. One fan’s clip turned the attention to Valkyries forward Janelle Salaün, who did not play in Game 7. Another fan wrote later Saturday night: “Also the WNBA fans make sure Cathy Engelbert knows how they feel about her!” Saturday was not the first time Engelbert heard it from a WNBA crowd. At the 2025 All-Star Game in Indianapolis, fans chanted “pay them” as she tried to deliver her postgame speech. She was heckled again during the trophy ceremony at the 2025 Finals. Earlier this season, at the 2026 Commissioner’s Cup championship at Barclays Center, her voice was almost entirely drowned out when she took the microphone after New York beat Las Vegas. The reaction carried into Sunday. One fan, posting that morning, went further: “She 100% deserves it. She might be a nice person I have no idea but she is in so far over her head trying to run the league it is sad.” The league has described Engelbert’s tenure in different terms. Announcing her retirement on September 4, NBA commissioner Adam Silver said she “has presided over the WNBA through the most significant period of growth in the league’s 30-year history.” The announcement credited her with steep gains in viewership, attendance, and franchise valuations, both reaching historic highs, as well as a program of charter flights for teams. She played a part, it said, in negotiating the agreements reached through collective bargaining, deals that produced pay raises of historic size for players. She also oversaw the league’s largest expansion to date, growing it to 18 teams by 2030, up from 12. That growth includes the Valkyries, awarded to the Bay Area three years ago. READ MORE: ‘Angel Reese Is 0-1 in the Finals,’ ‘Thank You, Gabby Williams’ – Dave Portnoy, Caitlin Clark Fans Troll Dream Star After Game 7 Loss Engelbert was appointed the league’s first commissioner in 2019. In the same announcement, she said, “After more than seven years at the WNBA and more than 40 total years in business, I have made the decision to retire as WNBA Commissioner.” She added, “I retire knowing we have built something bigger, stronger and more enduring than we could have imagined.” The NBA has hired Excel Search & Advisory, Excel Sports Management’s executive search firm, to lead the search for her successor, and Silver will choose her replacement together with the WNBA Board of Governors. item.title: Penguins Defenseman Makes Surprising Admission After Crosby’s Historic Game
item.description: LAS VEGAS, NEVADA - OCTOBER 17: Spencer Stastney #24 of the Pittsburgh Penguins shoots the puck against the Vegas Golden Knights during the game at T-Mobile Arena on October 17, 2026 in Las Vegas, Nevada. The Golden Knights defeated the Penguins 6-2. (Photo by Christian Petersen/Getty Images) Getty The Pittsburgh Penguins allowed five goals in their loss to the Montreal Canadiens, but it didn’t stop Sidney Crosby from making history. Per NHL.com’s Sean Farrell, “Sidney Crosby scored with 3:11 remaining in the third period to draw the Penguins within 5-4 and tie Marcel Dionne for sixth on the NHL points list with 1,771.” That was impressive, and it further solidifies Crosby’s status as arguably an eventual top-five player in league history. But defenseman Spencer Stastney’s comments regarding Crosby following the game made the milestone more memorable. Stastney said, “It’s crazy. I grew up with a Fathead of him on my wall.” In many ways, it’s a reminder of how long Crosby has been in the league. His career dates back to the 2005-06 season. So, many players like Stastney grew up watching and idolizing players like Crosby. It is a bonus for these players to be skating alongside Crosby and become part of his latest records and milestones. In Stastney’s case, he was five years old when the Penguins drafted Crosby. Stastney was drafted in 2018 when the Nashville Predators selected him in the fifth round. By then, Crosby had been a cornerstone for the Penguins for the past 13 seasons. Crosby’s Milestones Are Just Part Of The Story For The 2026-27 Penguins While it is satisfying for players like Stastney to get a front-row seat as Crosby continues to rewrite the history books, it would be even better if it translated into another playoff berth. Now in his age-39 season, Crosby won’t be in the league much longer. So it’s up to players like Stastney to do all they can to help the Penguins get back into the playoffs as Crosby, Evgeni Malkin, and Kris Letang enter their career twilight. That won’t be a simple task after Pittsburgh allowed five goals against the Canadiens. Pittsburgh may rank in the middle of the league with 46 goals scored, but goaltending has been an issue all season. That said, they haven’t been completing sequences as well as they should. Pittsburgh heads into November with 35.9 expected goals for (xGF) at 5-on-5 but has scored just 31 times. Their expected goals allowed (xGA) is 31.8 in the same situation. But they have watched 35 cross into the net. At some point, finishing sequences and preventing opponents from finishing sequences at 5-on-5 must improve if the youth movement wants to give veterans like Crosby another chance at the Stanley Cup. Pittsburgh also finds itself in sixth place in the Metropolitan Division with 12 points. That puts them three points behind the fifth-place New York Rangers . item.title: Is DJ Moore playing vs. Ravens? Final Week 8 injury update
item.description: Gregory Fisher-Imagn Images Is DJ Moore playing vs. Ravens? Final Week 8 injury update appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Buffalo Bills are one of the NFL’s best teams headed into Week 8 . Buffalo is 5-1 coming out of their bye week and looking to create some distance from New England in the AFC East standings. That task will not be easy while going up against the Baltimore Ravens on Sunday. Ravens QB Lamar Jackson will finally return from injury , which completely changes Baltimore’s offense. Now the Bills will face an incredibly tough game against another AFC superpower in front of their home crowd. This game could easily have a playoff atmosphere to match the excellent matchup on the field. That means one of Buffalo’s biggest priorities should be fielding as many players as possible. Fortunately, the Bills did receive some positive injury news this week. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Moore just received an injury update that Bills fans will want to see before Sunday’s game against the Ravens. DJ Moore ’s injury status vs. Ravens Mark Konezny-Imagn Images Moore is expected to play against the Ravens after missing the last two games with a shoulder injury, per ESPN’s Adam Schefter. The 29-year-old wide receiver has yet to string together multiple productive games since joining the Bills. He started off hot with five receptions for 100 receiving yards and a touchdown in Week 1. Since then, he’s dealt with multiple injuries, including this shoulder problem. Moore could not have picked a better time to return to the starting lineup. Buffalo will need all the firepower they can bring to bear with Lamar Jackson returning for Baltimore in Week 8. In other Bills injury news, ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reported that Dalton Kincaid is optimistic about playing on Sunday. He is officially listed as questionable with a chest injury. Bills vs. Ravens kicks off at 1 p.m. ET from Highmark Stadium in Buffalo. item.title: Barcelona star addresses Manchester United links
item.description: Barcelona star addresses Manchester United links Barcelona star Fermín López has issued a response to the surprise recent speculation linking him with a move to the Premier League, with struggling Manchester United. Midfielder Fermín is for his part in the midst of what has been another thoroughly productive opening to the new campaign. Just last night, the Spanish international secured Man of the Match honours, after notching a goal and two assists en route to a 6-1 Barca drubbing of Deportivo Alavés. This took Fermín’s season tally to 12 direct goal contributions in 13 appearances between La Liga and the Champions League. Amid an ongoing search for added dynamism in their engine room ranks, the aforementioned Manchester United are in turn understood to have earmarked Barca’s all-action midfielder as the ideal profile. Speaking to the media in the aftermath of his side’s victory over Alavés on Saturday, however, Fermín was keen to play down his Old Trafford links: “Manchester United links? I don’t pay attention to that kind of news. I want to stay here at Barça as long as possible. I hope to end my football career at this club and retire here.” Conor Laird – GSFN

item.title: Chinese state TV fails to air Real Madrid match after Mbappe row
item.description: Real Madrid forward Kylian Mbappe scored in Sunday's La Liga clash against Racing Santander, but viewers in China were unable to see the goal after state broadcaster CCTV did not broadcast the match (ANDER GILLENEA) Chinese state broadcaster CCTV did not broadcast a Real Madrid La Liga match on Sunday after star forward Kylian Mbappe caused a furore in China with remarks he made about former leader Mao Zedong. The match between Real Madrid and Racing Santander began at 1515 GMT but was not broadcast on either of CCTV's two sports channels, AFP reporters saw. None of the other matches from the 11th round of La Liga have been broadcast live on public television so far. A viral video in recent days showed Mbappe referring to Mao as a "dictator", prompting the body overseeing CCTV to say it would halt broadcasts of the top Spanish league. Mbappe, Real and La Liga later all said sorry for his remarks, and China's foreign ministry said it took the player's apology "seriously". Asked by AFP before the weekend, La Liga said that Chinese television had previously shown all games live, without specifying which platforms hosted the broadcasts. AFP journalists did find live broadcasts of matches on Migu, a digital streaming service owned by the state-owned China Mobile telecom network. That included Barcelona's 6-1 win over Alaves on Saturday. However, the Racing Santander–Real Madrid match did not appear to be broadcast on Sunday on Migu. China Media Group (CMG), which oversees CCTV, had said it had moved on Monday to suspend La Liga broadcasts, adding that apologies from La Liga, Mbappe and Real Madrid were "an absolute prerequisite" for moving past the furore. The viral video showed Mbappe saying that the funniest internet meme about him he had seen was of his face photoshopped onto that of "some guy -- I think he's a Chinese dictator". This was an apparent reference to a meme of Mbappe superimposed on an image of Mao. Mbappe later apologised for his "ill-judged" comments, La Liga said it "deeply" regretted them, and Real followed suit. CCTV's sports website later reported that CMG had acknowledged the apologies, but it remains unclear whether talks to defuse the situation have begun. China is a huge market for European football, with CCTV also carrying matches from the Premier League as well as the German, French and Italian top flights. Real Madrid coach Jose Mourinho said on Saturday that the club had "done our part" to put the controversy behind them. It is taboo in China to crack jokes about Mao, who died in 1976 and whose drastic policies are blamed by historians for mass starvation and millions of deaths. Major Chinese brands cancelled sponsorship deals with Mbappe after his comments. Various overseas sports leagues and players have found themselves in hot water for comments on topics that are politically sensitive to China.
