AFP journalists did find live broadcasts of matches on Migu, a digital streaming service owned by the state-owned China Mobile telecom network. That included Barcelona's 6-1 win over Alaves on Saturday. However, the Racing Santander–Real Madrid match did not appear to be broadcast on Sunday on Migu. China Media Group (CMG), which oversees CCTV, had said it had moved on Monday to suspend La Liga broadcasts, adding that apologies from La Liga, Mbappe and Real Madrid were "an absolute prerequisite" for moving past the furore. The viral video showed Mbappe saying that the funniest internet meme about him he had seen was of his face photoshopped onto that of "some guy -- I think he's a Chinese dictator". This was an apparent reference to a meme of Mbappe superimposed on an image of Mao. Mbappe later apologised for his "ill-judged" comments, La Liga said it "deeply" regretted them, and Real followed suit. CCTV's sports website later reported that CMG had acknowledged the apologies, but it remains unclear whether talks to defuse the situation have begun. China is a huge market for European football, with CCTV also carrying matches from the Premier League as well as the German, French and Italian top flights. Real Madrid coach Jose Mourinho said on Saturday that the club had "done our part" to put the controversy behind them. It is taboo in China to crack jokes about Mao, who died in 1976 and whose drastic policies are blamed by historians for mass starvation and millions of deaths. Major Chinese brands cancelled sponsorship deals with Mbappe after his comments. Various overseas sports leagues and players have found themselves in hot water for comments on topics that are politically sensitive to China. China effectively cut ties with the NBA for several years from 2019 after then-Houston Rockets general manager Daryl Morey tweeted his support for Hong Kong protesters. ehl-bur/pbt/pi/mw

item.title: New York Jets vs Las Vegas Raiders: Breece Hall headlines Jets’ inactives
item.description: DETROIT,MICHIGAN-SEPTEMBER 27: Running back Breece Hall #20 of the New York Jets is checked for injury during the second half of an NFL football game between the New York Jets and the Detroit Lions in Detroit, Michigan USA, on Sunday, September 27, 2026 (Photo by Jorge Lemus/NurPhoto via Getty Images) | NurPhoto via Getty Images Breece Hall will not be suiting up for the New York Jets when they take on the Las Vegas Raiders today. Hall will be inactive for the fifth consecutive week after he suffered a quadriceps injury against the Detroit Lions in the Jets’ third game of the 2026 season. The Jets are hopeful Hall will finally get back into the lineup next week against the Kansas City Chiefs. Hall’s absence has created an opportunity for Braelon Allen at running back, and Allen has taken full advantage. In the four games Allen has started in Hall’s absence this season Allen has put together two 100+ rushing yards games. Overall, Allen has averaged 4.6 yards per carry this season while already posting career highs in rushing yards with 418 and yards from scrimmage with 493. Allen has arguably been a more effective back than Hall, and he has presumably earned a larger role in the Jets’ offense even when Hall is back in the lineup. The full Jets inactive list for today’s game is as follows: Breece Hall David Bailey Joseph Ossai Nahshon Wright Tim Patrick Kohl Levao Max Mitchell Notable among those names is Nahshon Wright. Wright signed with the Jets in the offseason after earning a Pro Bowl nod last year with the Chicago Bears. Unfortunately that signing has not worked out for Wright or the Jets. Wright has been active for just three games for the Jets. He has played just 22 snaps, all on special teams. It probably would behoove the Jets to move Wright at the trade deadline, assuming there is any market for him.

item.title: Nebraska HC Matt Rhule sends message to Huskers fans after third straight loss
item.description: Matt Rhule had a message for Nebraska Cornhuskers fans in his postgame news conference Saturday night, after the Washington Huskies won 17-10 at Memorial Stadium in Nebraska’s annual Blackout Game. The loss marked the third straight game in which Nebraska held a lead in the fourth quarter and walked off beaten. The skid has turned a 5-0 start into a 5-3 record, with the three losses coming by a combined 13 points. The No. 7 Indiana Hoosiers erased a 17-6 fourth-quarter deficit to win 20-17 on Oct. 10, the Oregon Ducks followed with a 17-14 win a week later, and Washington finished the set on Halloween night. “I certainly understand how frustrated everyone is that this has happened three games in a row. But all I can do is show up tomorrow and get back to work for Illinois,” Rhule said. Oct 11, 2025; College Park, Maryland, USA; Nebraska Cornhuskers head coach Matt Rhule walks on the field during the game against the Maryland Terrapins at SECU Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Tommy Gilligan-Imagn Images Washington finished with a season-low 267 yards and punted on eight of its nine possessions, and Nebraska carried a 7-3 lead into the fourth quarter. Kyle Cunanan then missed a 36-yard field goal that would have made it 10-3. Washington backup quarterback Demond Williams Jr., who entered early in the fourth quarter, kept the winning drive alive with a 24-yard completion to Chris Lawson on fourth-and-18. Lawson caught the go-ahead touchdown two plays later with 1:30 left. Anthony Colandrea’s third interception of the night was returned 48 yards for a touchdown by Alex McLaughlin on the next possession, and John Hohl’s 42-yard field goal with 31 seconds left only trimmed the margin. “Three turnovers and a missed field goal are not a recipe to win,” Rhule said. Matt Rhule shares his message to Nebraska fans after three straight losses. https://t.co/wSOb0BriNa — Hail Varsity (@HailVarsity) November 1, 2026 Why Matt Rhule’s fourth-quarter warning keeps coming true Oct 11, 2025; College Park, Maryland, USA; Nebraska Cornhuskers head coach Matt Rhule on the field before the game against the Maryland Terrapins at SECU Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Tommy Gilligan-Imagn Images Rhule identified the same issue at his Monday news conference on Oct. 19, two days after the Oregon loss. “We won’t win the games we want to win until we win the fourth quarter,” Rhule said. Nebraska had an open week before Washington and still lost the fourth quarter 14-3 to an offense that had punted on nearly every possession until then. Rhule’s message Saturday paired an acknowledgment of the frustration with a promise of work, and the fourth-quarter problem he described after Oregon has now cost Nebraska a third straight game it led late. Nebraska plays at the Illinois Fighting Illini on Friday at 8 p.m. ET on Fox. item.title: NFL rumors: How Myles Garrett trade helped get Jeffery Simmons deal over finish line for Bears, Titans
item.description: Steve Roberts-Imagn Images NFL rumors: How Myles Garrett trade helped get Jeffery Simmons deal over finish line for Bears, Titans appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Chicago Bears ’ blockbuster acquisition of Jeffery Simmons reportedly took shape because of another massive NFL trade. Chicago and the Tennessee Titans used the Myles Garrett deal as a blueprint for their negotiations, helping both sides agree on the defensive tackle’s value. The Bears had been searching for a defensive difference-maker, and Simmons emerged as their target. Tennessee initially resisted interest in its four-time Pro Bowler, who had signed a lucrative contract extension earlier this year. According to ESPN’s Adam Schefter, Bears general manager Ryan Poles contacted Titans GM Mike Borgonzi again Tuesday night. The teams then used the Garrett trade as their framework for determining compensation. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Cleveland previously received Jared Verse and three draft picks from the Los Angeles Rams for Garrett. Tennessee reportedly valued Verse as equivalent to a first-round selection when comparing the packages. That helped establish the price for Simmons. Chicago surrendered its 2027 and 2028 first-round picks, plus a 2027 fourth-rounder, while receiving Simmons and a 2028 fifth-round selection. The Titans also studied other blockbuster trades involving Matthew Stafford and Russell Wilson before deciding additional draft capital could accelerate their rebuild. Chicago approached the negotiations differently. The Bears examined recent Super Bowl champions and identified the importance of elite interior defensive linemen. Simmons fit that profile, giving Chicago an established presence alongside its existing defensive talent. For Tennessee, the return provides valuable flexibility as the franchise builds around its younger players. The organization had previously dismissed trade interest in Simmons. Ultimately, the Garrett deal helped both front offices settle on a price. Chicago gained an immediate defensive upgrade, while Tennessee secured premium draft assets for its future. Related: Bears rule out Kyle Monangai for Seahawks MNF showdown Related: Colston Loveland good to go, Kyle Monangai ruled out in Bears’ latest Week 8 injury report

item.title: Jaguars vs. Colts Week 8 inactives: Jonathan Taylor officially active
item.description: The Jacksonville Jaguars (4-2) enter Sunday's matchup against the Indianapolis Colts (2-5) with little in the way of mystery. As the Jaguars continue their season with Super Bowl aspirations, the Colts appear to be going in the opposite direction. Indianapolis traded two of their best franchise players: guard Quenton Nelson and defensive tackle DeForest Buckner . The team could still trade star running back Jonathan Taylor , but he was deemed active for the contest. Either way, a full rebuild is in store for the Colts, who also canned their general manager a couple of weeks ago. PREVIEW: Why Jaguars' 11 straight home wins vs Colts don't matter to Liam Coen Before the game, the Jaguars elevated linebacker Jamal Hill from their practice squad to the active roster via standard elevation. Hill was signed to the practice squad last week. Jaguars Week 8 inactives vs. Colts: Antonio Johnson ruled out ahead of game Before the game, the Jaguars announced that safety Antonio Johnson (ankle) would be ruled out for Sunday's contest. Johnson was injured during the team's Week 6 loss to the Houston Texans . Meanwhile, the franchise is welcoming back cornerback Montaric Brown, who missed Week 6 after re-injuring the ailment in Week 5 against the Philadelphia Eagles . Brown missed Week 4 with the same ailment. Despite being listed as questionable, wide receiver Jakobi Meyers (ankle/hamstring) is active. Jaguars Week 8 inactives vs. Colts: S Antonio Johnson WR CJ Williams CB Alijah Huzzie LB Jamal Hill DE Wesley Williams DT Albert Regis Jonathan Taylor set to play despite trade interest A storyline ahead of the contest on the opposite side of the field is Taylor's status and whether the team will offload him for picks a la Buckner and Nelson. So far, reports around the league have indicated the Colts are listening to offers and are willing to deal the back. But there's been no indication the Colts are shopping Taylor. They aren't desperate to move him. Because of the trade interest, many speculated whether Taylor would be active. Indy just answered that: they're keeping the franchise RB active for today's game against Jacksonville. The question remains: how much will Taylor play? item.title: Did Stephon Castle Get Hurt? Why Spurs’ Star Scored 0 Points vs. Timberwolves
item.description: NEW YORK, NEW YORK - JUNE 08: Stephon Castle #5 of the San Antonio Spurs handles the ball during the second quarter against the New York Knicks in Game Three of the 2026 NBA Finals at Madison Square Garden on June 08, 2026 in New York City. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this photograph, User is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. (Photo by Al Bello/Getty Images) Getty The San Antonio Spurs got the chance to take on a Minnesota Timberwolves team that is without an injured Anthony Edwards on Saturday. The Wolves are still talented, but this was a key opportunity for the Spurs to pick up a Western Conference win against a shorthanded foe. The Spurs didn’t pass that chance up. They took care of business in a 121-111 win on Saturday night. There was plenty of good from the Spurs, starting with a monster stat night from Victor Wembanyama. Wemby scored 43 points on 17-for-34 shooting from the floor, including 3-for-8 from deep, as well as 6-for-9 on free throws. He added seven rebounds, four assists, six blocks and a steal. The Spurs also got 25 points, seven rebounds and six assists out of Dylan Harper, and De’Aaron Fox had 22 points, eight rebounds and seven assists. The one oddity came from Stephon Castle: He didn’t score a point. Did Stephon Castle Get Hurt? Stephon Castle didn’t appear to get injured during Saturday’s game, but he did enter proceedings at less than 100%. The Spurs had added him to the injury report less than 24 hours before the game. He was listed as questionable due to a migraine. Castle did eventually get deemed available to play. Why Stephon Castle Scored 0 Points Whatever migraine Castle was dealing with couldn’t have helped, and he also got in a bit of foul trouble that stopped him from finding a rhythm. He ended up playing 22 minutes to score his 0 points. Castle shot 0-for-4 from the field, including 0-for-2 from 3-point range. He didn’t get to the foul line. At least Castle contributed five rebounds and four assists with a steal, although he did have three turnovers. The Spurs played Harper, Fox, Devin Vassell, Julian Champagnie and Keldon Johnson all big minutes. It seems they might’ve been aware all along that Castle might need a bit more time on the bench than usual. It’s going to be something worth watching with Castle going forward, both in the short-term and long-term. The first thing is simply whether Castle is listed on the injury report before the next game, because that suggests this is something the Spurs might have to manage. Migraines can also re-emerge later on as an issue, so if that’s something that nags Castle going forward, it’s certainly less than ideal. For now, the Spurs can feel good they got a nice win, and Castle can do his best to recover and recharge before the next time out. This article was originally published on HEAVY The post Did Stephon Castle Get Hurt? Why Spurs’ Star Scored 0 Points vs. Timber

item.title: Bengals Get Major Update on Potential Blockbuster Trade for Saquon Barkley
item.description: CINCINNATI, OHIO - OCTOBER 27: Saquon Barkley #26 of the Philadelphia Eagles runs onto the field prior to the game against the Cincinnati Bengals at Paycor Stadium on October 27, 2024 in Cincinnati, Ohio. (Photo by Andy Lyons/Getty Images) Getty The Cincinnati Bengals‘ run game has been underwhelming through their first six games this season. There’s a lot that factors into it. There’s no secret that Cincinnati is a pass-first team and would be regardless of who’s in the backfield. When you have Joe Burrow at quarterback with wide receivers like Ja’Marr Chase and Tee Higgins on the outside, you’re going to want to throw the ball. At the same time, Cincinnati has really struggled when trying to establish the run with Chase Brown or Samaje Perine. With the trade deadline set for Nov. 10, rumors have circulated about the Bengals potentially targeting a running back. Cincinnati has been linked to several running back targets, including Indianapolis Colts RB Jonathan Taylor and Philadelphia Eagles star Saquon Barkley. Bengals Get Major Update on Barkley A trade for either player would be a blockbuster, and on Saturday, we found out that the Colts are truly open to moving Taylor. As for Barkley, despite the Eagles sitting at 2-5, NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo and Ian Rapoport revealed Sunday morning that Philadelphia has no intention of trading the star running back. Via ESPN.com : “Saquon Barkley will not be traded before next week’s trade deadline, sources told NFL Network, putting an end to speculation that the star running back could be on the move with the Philadelphia Eagles trending toward being out of contention.” Is Barkley Playing on Sunday Night? The Eagles will travel to Washington to take on the Commanders in a massive divisional matchup that could have major implications for their season. As of now, all indications point to Barkley being active and ready to go. He made it clear that playing wasn’t much of a question when speaking to the media Friday. “One day I’m not going to be playing football. Whenever that is, I don’t want to look back and be like, ‘I could’ve gave it a chance and I didn’t,'” Barkley said. “I like playing football. So if I have an opportunity to play, I’m going to try my best to play.” This article was originally published on HEAVY The post Bengals Get Major Update on Potential Blockbuster Trade for Saquon Barkley appeared first on HEAVY .

item.title: Lions, Vikings Week 8 inactives: Roger McCreary WILL PLAY
item.description: DETROIT, MICHIGAN - OCTOBER 25: Roger McCreary #21 of the Detroit Lions competes during fourth quarter of a game against the Green Bay Packers at Ford Field on October 25, 2026 in Detroit, Michigan. (Photo by Mike Mulholland/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Detroit Lions have declared their inactives ahead of their Week 8 matchup with divisional rival Minnesota Vikings, and Lions starting corner Roger McCreary is active and will play in this game. McCreary was a late addition to Friday’s injury report, being listed as questionable after having a limited practice with a foot injury, but the injury is not significant enough to keep him from contributing. If you missed this week’s roster transactions or need a refresher, we’ve got you covered with our updated depth chart, with position-by-position rankings and a visual overview . We also delivered a plethora of game previews leading up to this game, including my breakdowns of the Vikings’ offensive/defensive schemes and Honolulu Blueprint: Predictions for a victory , an On Paper preview from Jeremy Reisman, three key matchups to watch from Anthony Balaj, five key stats to know from Al Karsten, 5 questions preview from Ryan Mathews, our POD staff pick-em predictions from Brandon Knapp, and our fans pick-a-winner survey results . The Lions’ game-day roster sits at 53 players. With 48 players eligible to play, Detroit needs to declare five players inactive for today’s matchup. Lions inactives: TE Jackson Meeks C Seth McLaughlin EDGE Ahmed Hassanein DL Mekhi Wingo S Bishop Fitzgerald Vikings inactives: QB Max Brosmer (emergency 3rd QB) RB Demond Claiborne OL Caleb Tiernan DL Elijah Williams CB Charles Demmings S Jakobe Thomas

item.title: 🚨XIs confirmed: Relegation derby at the Martínez Valero
item.description: 🚨XIs confirmed: Relegation derby at the Martínez Valero The Martínez Valero hosts a demanding LaLiga clash between Elche and Valencia this Sunday. Martín Anselmi's Elche head into the game buoyed by a 3-0 thrashing of Rayo Vallecano, extending their unbeaten run to four matches with three clean sheets, although Fer Niño remains a doubt. Meanwhile, Javier Aguirre's Valencia are struggling to find their way: still mired in the relegation zone with just one win, they urgently need a response after losing to Villarreal. Thomas Lemar and Javi Guerra promise a decisive battle in midfield. Confirmed line-ups This article was translated into English by Artificial Intelligence. item.title: Buffalo Bills Week 8 inactives vs. the Baltimore Ravens
item.description: LAS VEGAS, NV - OCTOBER 18: Dee Alford #23 of the Buffalo Bills lines up before the snap during an NFL football game against the Las Vegas Raiders at Allegiant Stadium on October 18, 2026 in Las Vegas, Nevada. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Buffalo Bills and the Baltimore Ravens are set to face off in what is a huge AFC matchup. With a win, the Bills move to 6-1 and maintain their edge over the New England Patriots in the AFC East. With a loss, they lose pace not only with New England, but with the Kansas City Chiefs in the race for the AFC’s top overall seed. Baltimore’s stakes are higher. Presently, they are 4-3, but they find themselves in fourth place in a surprisingly strong AFC North division. A win moves them to 5-3 and puts them right in the thick of things. However, a loss drops them to 4-4 and, depending on some other AFC results, could put them in a terrible position in the first week of November. Both teams have some key players returning from injury this week, but both teams also have key contributors who won’t be available. Here are the inactive players for each team this week. _____________________________________________________________________________ WR Skyler Bell After suiting up in the last two games thanks to DJ Moore’s absence, Bell is back to a healthy scratch with Moore returning. Joshua Palmer, who also missed Buffalo’s last game with an injury, is healthy and active this week, as well. T Spencer Brown After tweaking his back in practice this week, Brown was listed as questionable. Now, we know he’s out. Tylan Grable will likely start in his place. Rookie Jude Bowry is active for the first time this season. G Ar’Maj Reed-Adams The rookie seventh-round pick is once again a healthy scratch. DL Greg Gaines The veteran injured his calf in practice this week, and while he was listed as questionable, he’s not going to play today. Fortunately for Buffalo, Ed Oliver is back in action. OLB Mike Danna Rookie T.J. Parker was listed as quesitonable, so there was at least a shot that the veteran Danna would play this week. However, Parker is going to play, so Danna is once again a healthy scratch. CB Dee Alford With yesterday’s practice squad elevations of Geno Stone and A.J. Woods, as well as the signing of Te’Cory Couch to the active roster, this was something we expected. Couch will likely see plenty of time in the slot, although Woods is definitely an option there, as well. S Jalon Kilgore Looks like it’s Damar Hamlin and Geno Stone at safety to replace CJ Gardner-Johnson this week. I thought Kilgore would have an opportunity this week. I thought incorrectly. Gameday roster & inactives ⬇️ pic.twitter.com/K6ZOaTRtjS — Buffalo Bills PR (@BuffaloBillsPR) November 1, 2026 Here are the inactive players for Baltimore: Inactives at Bills pic.twitter.com/cZ2SXuPzbP — Baltimore Ravens (@Ravens) November 1, 2026

item.title: NDLEA intercepts large consignments of illicit drugs in 7 states
item.description: The National Drug Law Enforcement Agency (NDLEA) has intercepted large consignments of illicit drugs in seven states across the country. The states include Lagos, Kano, Kaduna, Sokoto, Ondo, Oyo and Edo, in a series of intelligence-led operations. This is contained in a statement by the Director, Media and Advocacy, NDLEA, Mr Femi Babafemi on Sunday in Abuja. Breaking down the operation, Babafemi said NDLEA operatives, acting on actionable intelligence about the movement of skunk, intercepted a white Volkswagen LT 28 bus along Kudirat Abiola Way, Ikeja, Lagos. Babafemi said the NDLEA operatives intercepted 537kg of skunk, a potent strain of cannabis, on Sunday, Oct. 25, while it was being transported from the Island to the Mainland. “The same day, another team of officers intercepted a brown J5 bus along the Gbagada–Oshodi expressway, with 439 kilograms of the same substance seized,”he said. In Oyo, NDLEA operatives on Thursday conducted a follow-up operation at Idere road, Igboora, where two suspects were arrested. Babafemi said that their arrest came while loading 554 kilograms of skunk into a Volvo truck for onward movement into town. “The operation targeted a notorious drug dealer known as ‘Omo Oba’, who escaped arrest on October 25. “This happened when officers seized 309.5 kilograms of the strong cannabis strain popularly called ‘Ghanaian Loud’ linked to him,” he said. Also, in Kano, NDLEA operatives on Monday raided a location in Tsamiya area of Gezawa where they recovered 247,500 tablets of diazepam weighing 57.7 kilograms and 100,000 tablets of Exol-5 weighing 38.7 kilograms. “Two days later, on Wednesday, October 28, another team of officers stormed Dorayi area of the state, where they arrested two suspects with 19,250 pills of tramadol 225mg weighing 13.6 kilograms,” Babafemi said. According to him, in a raid at Tashan Banke area of the state, officers also arrested seven suspects and recovered 178.85 kilograms of cannabis alongside quantities of diazepam, tramadol, Exol-5 and pregabalin. In Ondo State, NDLEA operatives, on Oct. 25 acting on credible intelligence, raided cannabis farms in Ijare forest. Babafemi said that they arrested four suspects, adding that a total of 16 bags of processed cannabis weighing 180 kilograms were recovered from the farms. Similarly, a team of NDLEA operatives supported by soldiers on Wednesday raided Eko Camp in Ilushi, Esan South East Local Government Area of Edo State. Babafemi said that a cannabis plantation measuring 1.646 hectares with an estimated yield of 4,115.53 kilograms was destroyed. “A 50-year-old woman was arrested at the camp with 301 kilograms of processed cannabis, while another 176 kilograms of the drug was recovered during the raid,”he said. In Sokoto, operatives of Zone 7 Command of NDLEA, acting on credible intelligence, on Saturday arrested a 68-year-old man with 236.6 kilograms of skunk The post NDLEA intercepts large consignments of illicit drugs in 7 states appeared first on Van

item.title: China’s State TV snubs Real Madrid match amid Mbappé controversy
item.description: Chinese state broadcaster CCTV did not broadcast a Real Madrid La Liga match on Sunday after star forward Kylian Mbappe caused a furore in China with remarks he made about former leader Mao Zedong. The match between Real Madrid and Racing Santander began at 1515 GMT but was not broadcast on either of CCTV’s two sports channels, AFP reporters saw. None of the other matches from the 11th round of La Liga have been broadcast live on public television so far. The post China’s State TV snubs Real Madrid match amid Mbappé controversy appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: A fully playable version of Portal prequel F-Stop leaked
item.description: Leakers have pieced together a playable version of the canceled Portal prequel F-Stop . Most of the assets came from the massive 12-terabyte leak that dropped this August. That didn't include the game's source code or map data, but those final pieces apparently hit the Valve Cut Content Discord this week, allowing a nearly complete version to be pieced together. Some dialog and elements of F-Stop eventually found their way into Portal 2 . But it differs dramatically from the mainline Portal games in that it's built around a camera mechanic that lets you capture an item by taking its picture and place it elsewhere using the resulting Polaroid … Read the full story at The Verge.

item.title: Scottish roundup: Falkirk shock Celtic; Rangers into Premier Sports Cup final
item.description: Celtic slumped to a 2-0 defeat at Falkirk on Sunday to ramp up the scrutiny on manager Martin O’Neill after a run of three wins in 10 games. The Scottish champions had the chance to extend their lead at the top of the table to seven points, but never recovered from conceding a third-minute opener to Ethan Ross. Scott Tanser slammed in a second before half-time and the Bairns even had a third goal ruled out by a VAR review for handball against Jacob Murrell. The majority of Celtic’s struggles this season have come in European competition as they crashed out of the Champions League qualifiers and have lost all three Europa League group matches. Continue reading...

item.title: 2027: Stick to your timetable, APC urges INEC
item.description: To take advantage of 13m members, 31 governors, 88 senators, 208 Reps. Demands equal media access, venues for all parties By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA: The ruling All Progressives Congress APC has urged the Independent National Electoral Commission INEC to adhere strictly to its published timetable for the 2027 general elections, insisting that the rules must apply equally to every political party. APC national chairman, Prof. Nentawe Goshwe Yilwatda, made the demand while receiving a pre-election fact-finding mission of the Economic Community of West African States ECOWAS at the party’s National Secretariat in Abuja. Special Adviser to the National Chairman on Media and Information Strategy, Mr Abimbola Tooki, in a statement on Sunday in Abuja, said Yilwatda received the mission, led by former Vice-President of Sierra Leone, Victor Bockarie Foh, with members of the National Working Committee NWC. “We believe INEC should stick to its timetable. The rules must apply equally to every political party. The electoral process must be fair, transparent and predictable, without adjusting deadlines in a manner that gives any party an undue advantage,” Yilwatda said. He said the APC had already released its campaign council list, inaugurated the council, commenced campaign activities and uploaded its candidates to the INEC portal ahead of its rivals. According to him, the party has presented candidates for all the elective positions it is contesting, in contrast to the difficulties some opposition parties reportedly encountered in fielding candidates and completing their submission processes. He said APC’s organisational strength placed it ahead of other parties. “Our party is the largest political party in Nigeria. In terms of structure, organisation and membership, no other political party comes close to us. We are approximately three times larger than the next political party in the country,” he said. He disclosed that the party has approximately 13 million registered members in all local government areas, with membership identity cards designed to allow verification through their National Identification Numbers NIN and voter identification details. The chairman added that the APC has more than 261,000 executive members across its structures from the ward to the national level. On elected offices, he said the party has 31 governors out of 36, 88 senators out of the 109-member Senate, and 208 members of the House of Representatives out of 360 seats. He added that the party also has a significant presence in state Houses of Assembly. “These structures are the foundation of our strength. We have built an organisation that reaches every part of the country and gives us the capacity to engage Nigerians across different demographics,” he said. Yilwatda said more than 7,000 aspirants contested for various positions in the party’s primaries, yet it recorded relatively few post-primary court cases compared with the scale of the contests. Demands equal media access, venues for all parties By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA: The ruling All Progressives Congress APC has urged the Independent National Electoral Commission INEC to adhere strictly to its published timetable for the 2027 general elections, insisting that the rules must apply equally to every political party. APC national chairman, Prof. Nentawe Goshwe Yilwatda, made the demand while receiving a pre-election fact-finding mission of the Economic Community of West African States ECOWAS at the party’s National Secretariat in Abuja. Special Adviser to the National Chairman on Media and Information Strategy, Mr Abimbola Tooki, in a statement on Sunday in Abuja, said Yilwatda received the mission, led by former Vice-President of Sierra Leone, Victor Bockarie Foh, with members of the National Working Committee NWC. “We believe INEC should stick to its timetable. The rules must apply equally to every political party. The electoral process must be fair, transparent and predictable, without adjusting deadlines in a manner that gives any party an undue advantage,” Yilwatda said. He said the APC had already released its campaign council list, inaugurated the council, commenced campaign activities and uploaded its candidates to the INEC portal ahead of its rivals. According to him, the party has presented candidates for all the elective positions it is contesting, in contrast to the difficulties some opposition parties reportedly encountered in fielding candidates and completing their submission processes. He said APC’s organisational strength placed it ahead of other parties. “Our party is the largest political party in Nigeria. In terms of structure, organisation and membership, no other political party comes close to us. We are approximately three times larger than the next political party in the country,” he said. He disclosed that the party has approximately 13 million registered members in all local government areas, with membership identity cards designed to allow verification through their National Identification Numbers NIN and voter identification details. The chairman added that the APC has more than 261,000 executive members across its structures from the ward to the national level. On elected offices, he said the party has 31 governors out of 36, 88 senators out of the 109-member Senate, and 208 members of the House of Representatives out of 360 seats. He added that the party also has a significant presence in state Houses of Assembly. “These structures are the foundation of our strength. We have built an organisation that reaches every part of the country and gives us the capacity to engage Nigerians across different demographics,” he said. Yilwatda said more than 7,000 aspirants contested for various positions in the party’s primaries, yet it recorded relatively few post-primary court cases compared with the scale of the contests. He observed that several politicians who failed to secure APC tickets later obtained tickets from opposition parties, including the African Democratic Congress ADC and the Nigeria Democratic Congress NDC. He said this underscored the intensity of competition for the APC’s tickets. Yilwatda, however, drew a line between size and dominance. “Being the largest political party does not mean that we want to suppress anybody. We want a democratic environment in which every party can organise, campaign and seek the support of Nigerians without fear,” he said. The chairman stressed that the party’s preparation was based on its organisational capacity, candidate readiness and nationwide structures, not on an assumption that victory was automatic. He assured the ECOWAS mission that the APC would not use its position to suppress opposition parties, and said all parties should enjoy equal access to the media, campaign venues and other legitimate opportunities to present their programmes to the electorate. Yilwatda cited public protests against the administration of President Bola Tinubu, including the “Tinubu Must Go” demonstrations, as evidence that citizens and opposition groups could express their views without being automatically subjected to arrest or intimidation. He also pointed to the political realignments that followed the APC’s defeat in the Anambra and Osun governorship elections. He said the party engaged stakeholders after those losses, and that the engagements contributed to broader alliances in support of Tinubu’s re-election bid. Earlier, Foh explained that the mission was undertaking a political assessment aimed at contributing to free, fair and transparent elections in Nigeria. “Our monitoring is scientific, and our decisions on issues are based on scientific observation. We verify information before making any pronouncement, and we use a robust application system to collect data. Our reports are therefore not arbitrary,” he said. Foh commended Yilwatda for his detailed presentation, saying it gave the mission valuable insight into the APC’s structure, membership, internal processes and preparations for the elections. The post 2027: Stick to your timetable, APC urges INEC appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Atiku tackles APC over Tinubu’s power pledge, says bonds can’t light homes
item.description: By Luminous Jannamike ABUJA – Former Vice President Atiku Abubakar has challenged the All Progressives Congress Presidential Campaign Council, APC-PCC, over its defence of President Bola Tinubu’s electricity pledge, insisting that Nigerians cannot power their homes and businesses with laws, bonds and project announcements. Atiku said despite the administration’s explanations about reforms and ongoing projects, Nigerians were still battling unreliable electricity, rising tariffs and the cost of alternative power, three and a half years after Tinubu promised steady supply and an end to estimated billing. In a statement on Sunday by the Director of Strategic Communication of the African Democratic Congress Presidential Campaign Council, ADC-PCC, Phrank Shaibu, the former vice president accused the APC campaign council of celebrating policy documents and financial interventions instead of addressing the failure to translate them into reliable electricity. “The APC should spare Nigerians the spectacle of celebrating paperwork while homes and businesses remain in darkness. After three and a half years, families still struggle to keep their homes lit. Traders and small business owners spend scarce resources on alternative power, yet struggle to keep their businesses alive. Nigerians are billed for electricity they cannot rely on. President Tinubu promised steady power and an end to estimated billing. That promise has not been kept,” he said. Atiku also faulted the electricity band system, arguing that consumers were paying different tariffs without corresponding improvements in supply. He cited Band A tariffs of about N209.50 per unit in many areas, before VAT, to illustrate the burden on consumers, insisting that Nigerians across all five bands continued to pay for electricity they could not reliably access. “No family should have to weigh the cost of electricity against the cost of food. No business should be left to pay more while receiving less,” he said. The former vice president also demanded clarity on the Federal Government’s plan to end electricity subsidies from 2027, questioning what the move would mean for household and business electricity bills. Atiku said despite the administration’s explanations about reforms and ongoing projects, Nigerians were still battling unreliable electricity, rising tariffs and the cost of alternative power, three and a half years after Tinubu promised steady supply and an end to estimated billing. In a statement on Sunday by the Director of Strategic Communication of the African Democratic Congress Presidential Campaign Council, ADC-PCC, Phrank Shaibu, the former vice president accused the APC campaign council of celebrating policy documents and financial interventions instead of addressing the failure to translate them into reliable electricity. “The APC should spare Nigerians the spectacle of celebrating paperwork while homes and businesses remain in darkness. After three and a half years, families still struggle to keep their homes lit. Traders and small business owners spend scarce resources on alternative power, yet struggle to keep their businesses alive. Nigerians are billed for electricity they cannot rely on. President Tinubu promised steady power and an end to estimated billing. That promise has not been kept,” he said. Atiku also faulted the electricity band system, arguing that consumers were paying different tariffs without corresponding improvements in supply. He cited Band A tariffs of about N209.50 per unit in many areas, before VAT, to illustrate the burden on consumers, insisting that Nigerians across all five bands continued to pay for electricity they could not reliably access. “No family should have to weigh the cost of electricity against the cost of food. No business should be left to pay more while receiving less,” he said. The former vice president also demanded clarity on the Federal Government’s plan to end electricity subsidies from 2027, questioning what the move would mean for household and business electricity bills. He proposed working with state governments and regulators to abolish the existing band system and introduce what he described as a fairer, more affordable framework that would hold power companies accountable for electricity delivered. Atiku’s lampooned the administration’s multitrillion-naira bond programme to settle legacy debts owed to generation companies, which he said could not be mistaken for investment in new electricity generation infrastructure. He alleged that the Tinubu administration had not built any new generation infrastructure of its own to expand Nigeria’s power capacity. “Paying old debts is not the same as building new power infrastructure. Bonds cannot be presented as a substitute for power in people’s homes,” he said. He also raised concerns over VAT on electricity and the five per cent surcharge provided for certain fossil fuels, including petrol and diesel, under the Nigeria Tax Act, arguing that Nigerians already struggling with energy costs deserved clarity on the prospect of additional charges. The ADC-PCC’s response followed a defence by APC-PCC spokesman, Dele Alake, who had described the power sector reforms as ongoing work and cited the Electricity Act 2023, a N4 trillion bond programme to settle verified debts owed to generation and gas companies, metering initiatives, transmission projects and state electricity reforms as evidence of the administration’s efforts. But Atiku insisted that the government could not substitute financial commitments and policy announcements for measurable improvements in electricity supply. “Dele Alake’s statement cannot light a home. Signing a law is not electricity. Raising a bond is not electricity. Approving a project is not power delivered. Nigerians cannot cook, study, work or sustain a business on announcements.” He then returned to the President’s own campaign promise ahead of the 2023 election. “If I don’t give you constant electricity for four years, when I come back for a second term, don’t vote for me.” Atiku said Nigerians had now lived through the period Tinubu set for himself and should no longer be asked to accept explanations from his campaign council. “They do not need his campaign council to interpret his words for them. They need him to answer for them,” he said. The post Atiku tackles APC over Tinubu’s power pledge, says bonds can’t light homes appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: FG launches USSD service to help Nigerians access loans without internet [How to apply]
item.description: The Federal Government has launched a new USSD-based credit service, SPARK, designed to help Nigerians access loans and build formal credit histories using basic mobile phones. The product, introduced by the Nigerian Consumer Credit Corporation (CREDICORP), targets Nigerians, particularly first-time borrowers who have limited or no credit history. Interested Nigerians can dial *347*333# on their mobile phones to access the service without requiring a smartphone or internet connection. According to CREDICORP, SPARK is designed to simplify access to consumer credit while helping beneficiaries establish repayment records that could improve their credit profiles and open up further financial opportunities. “By establishing repayment records through responsible borrowing, beneficiaries can progressively improve their credit profiles and create pathways to greater financial opportunities,” the corporation said. It added that the product is expected to become more widely available to Nigerians before the end of 2026. Why FG introduced SPARK The product was unveiled at CREDICORP’s ‘CREDICORP for All’ showcase in Aba, Abia State, where the corporation highlighted affordable credit opportunities for more than 1,000 residents. The event brought together beneficiaries, participating financial institutions, local vendors and government representatives to demonstrate how consumer credit could support businesses and improve livelihoods. Activities included credit-access demonstrations for market women and traders, presentations on the YouthCred initiative for young Nigerians, and the showcasing of credit-backed tricycles for transport operators. The event also featured locally assembled tricycles made available on credit through CREDICORP’s Securing Consumer Access for Local Enterprises (S.C.A.L.E.) initiative. CREDICORP Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer, Uzoma Nwagba, said the initiative was designed to make consumer credit accessible beyond traditional financial institutions. “Consumer credit should not be a privilege reserved for a few. It should be an opportunity available to every working Nigerian,” he said. He added, “Today in Aba, Abia State, in Nigeria’s South East, we are demonstrating what that means in practical terms: credit for market women, a financial head start for young people, productive assets for transport operators, and with SPARK, a simple way for Nigerians to begin building their credit histories. This is how we make credit work for the people.” Chinenye Mba-Uzoukwu, chief principal to Abia State Governor Alex Otti, said the state government was creating an environment where responsible consumer credit and enterprise could thrive. “Under Governor Alex Otti’s leadership, Abia State is putting the conditions in place for businesses to grow, investments to flourish and responsible credit to reach more of our people,” Mba-Uzoukwu said, representing the governor at the event. “By strengthening the enabling environment for enterpris

The event brought together beneficiaries, participating financial institutions, local vendors and government representatives to demonstrate how consumer credit could support businesses and improve livelihoods. Activities included credit-access demonstrations for market women and traders, presentations on the YouthCred initiative for young Nigerians, and the showcasing of credit-backed tricycles for transport operators. The event also featured locally assembled tricycles made available on credit through CREDICORP’s Securing Consumer Access for Local Enterprises (S.C.A.L.E.) initiative. CREDICORP Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer, Uzoma Nwagba, said the initiative was designed to make consumer credit accessible beyond traditional financial institutions. “Consumer credit should not be a privilege reserved for a few. It should be an opportunity available to every working Nigerian,” he said. He added, “Today in Aba, Abia State, in Nigeria’s South East, we are demonstrating what that means in practical terms: credit for market women, a financial head start for young people, productive assets for transport operators, and with SPARK, a simple way for Nigerians to begin building their credit histories. This is how we make credit work for the people.” Chinenye Mba-Uzoukwu, chief principal to Abia State Governor Alex Otti, said the state government was creating an environment where responsible consumer credit and enterprise could thrive. “Under Governor Alex Otti’s leadership, Abia State is putting the conditions in place for businesses to grow, investments to flourish and responsible credit to reach more of our people,” Mba-Uzoukwu said, representing the governor at the event. “By strengthening the enabling environment for enterprise, we are making it easier for initiatives such as CREDICORP to support traders, young people and hardworking families across the state.” Similarly, Armstrong Ume Takang, Managing Director of the Ministry of Finance Incorporated (MOFI) and a CREDICORP board member, said the showcase demonstrated how Federal Government policies could translate into economic opportunities for Nigerians. “Through CREDICORP, we are seeing how well-structured public investment can stimulate enterprise, support local manufacturers and deliver measurable economic impact directly to citizens,” Takang said. CREDICORP said it had facilitated more than N53.5bn in consumer credit for over 351,000 Nigerians since commencing operations, with women accounting for approximately 59 per cent of beneficiaries. item.title: Planetary defense: How military and civil satellites are watching fireballs to help keep Earth safe from space rocks
item.description: null It came from outer space, exploding high above the South Atlantic off the coast of Argentina. That April 1 event — an incoming meteor , also termed a bolide — was observed by both U.S. space-based military and civil sensors. Hush-hush U.S. government satellite sensors detected the speedy fireball cutting through our atmosphere. The object's brightness peaked at an altitude of nearly 60 miles (90.5 kilometers) over the South Atlantic. That dazzling spectacle was also caught by the National Atmospheric and Oceanic Administration's GOES-E and Europe's Meteosat Third Generation (MTG) Imager-1 satellite. Those two independent spacecraft in geostationary orbit detected the bolide via onboard lightning imagers. This skyfall show is among a number of recent episodes that spotlight the value of combining multi-sensor data to not only portray fireball dynamics but also to help appreciate human-caused space debris impacts, as well as strengthening planetary defense knowhow. Hovering in a fixed position high above Earth's equator, the Meteosat Third Generation mission is designed to deliver a rapid stream of data for enhanced weather forecasting. Its Lightning Imager offers a completely new capability for European meteorological satellites, including bolide detection. (Image credit: ESA/Mlabspace) Catastrophic fragmentation Take, for instance, another extraterrestrial incident. In this case, an April 24, 2025 fireball over south-central Alaska yielded one of the most densely recorded "seismoacoustic" datasets ever obtained for a nature-made bolide en route to busting up. A network of 37 seismic stations, 16 single infrasound sensors, and four infrasound arrays recorded 30 ballistic and multiple fragmentation arrivals. All this was complemented by Doppler weather radar detections of falling meteorites and independent optical video observations. Now, toss in for good measure yet another encounter. A roughly 12-foot-wide (3.7 meters) space rock plowed through Earth's atmosphere over northwest Queensland, Australia, on May 20, 2023, accompanied by a raucous round of sonic booms. And U.S. government space-based sensors caught the fall . Researchers later determined that the object underwent catastrophic fragmentation, producing one of the 20 most energetic events reported by NASA's Center for Near-Earth Object Studies (CNEOS) since 1988 and the most energetic seen over Australia. It was equivalent to the explosion of a 7.1-kiloton bomb. An April 24, 2025 fireball event over south-central Alaska. Green stations denote sensors with detections. (Image credit: Scamfer, L. T., et al.) item.content:encoded: null It came from outer space, exploding high above the South Atlantic off the coast of Argentina. That April 1 event — an incoming meteor , also termed a bolide — was observed by both U.S. space-based military and civil sensors. Hush-hush U.S. government satellite sensors detected the speedy fireball cutting through our atmosphere. The object's brightness peaked at an altitude of nearly 60 miles (90.5 kilometers) over the South Atlantic. That dazzling spectacle was also caught by the National Atmospheric and Oceanic Administration's GOES-E and Europe's Meteosat Third Generation (MTG) Imager-1 satellite. Those two independent spacecraft in geostationary orbit detected the bolide via onboard lightning imagers. This skyfall show is among a number of recent episodes that spotlight the value of combining multi-sensor data to not only portray fireball dynamics but also to help appreciate human-caused space debris impacts, as well as strengthening planetary defense knowhow. Hovering in a fixed position high above Earth's equator, the Meteosat Third Generation mission is designed to deliver a rapid stream of data for enhanced weather forecasting. Its Lightning Imager offers a completely new capability for European meteorological satellites, including bolide detection. (Image credit: ESA/Mlabspace) Catastrophic fragmentation Take, for instance, another extraterrestrial incident. In this case, an April 24, 2025 fireball over south-central Alaska yielded one of the most densely recorded "seismoacoustic" datasets ever obtained for a nature-made bolide en route to busting up. A network of 37 seismic stations, 16 single infrasound sensors, and four infrasound arrays recorded 30 ballistic and multiple fragmentation arrivals. All this was complemented by Doppler weather radar detections of falling meteorites and independent optical video observations. Now, toss in for good measure yet another encounter. A roughly 12-foot-wide (3.7 meters) space rock plowed through Earth's atmosphere over northwest Queensland, Australia, on May 20, 2023, accompanied by a raucous round of sonic booms. And U.S. government space-based sensors caught the fall . Researchers later determined that the object underwent catastrophic fragmentation, producing one of the 20 most energetic events reported by NASA's Center for Near-Earth Object Studies (CNEOS) since 1988 and the most energetic seen over Australia. It was equivalent to the explosion of a 7.1-kiloton bomb. An April 24, 2025 fireball event over south-central Alaska. This illustration is a detection map showing a regional seismo-acoustic network in south-central and interior Alaska. Only stations with available data during the fireball event are shown. Green stations denote sensors with detections. (Image credit: Scamfer, L. T., et al.) Location, time and estimated energy "For many fireballs, U.S. Government detections reported through NASA's CNEOS database provide an important starting point by establishing that an event occurred and, in many cases, providing basic parameters such as location, time and estimated energy," explained Elizabeth Silber, a senior research and development physicist at the U.S. Department of Energy's Sandia National Laboratories in New Mexico. "Civil and scientific observing systems can then add independent measurements that help refine and validate that initial characterization," said Silber. CNEOS, which is based at the Jet Propulsion Laboratory in Southern California, is NASA's center for computing asteroid and comet orbits and their odds of striking Earth. CNEOS computes high-precision orbits for such objects in support of NASA's Planetary Defense Coordination Office. Different and complementary information "The Alaska event is an especially useful example, because it was not reported by U.S. Government sensors in the CNEOS database. In this case, the event was reconstructed almost entirely from civil and scientific observations," Silber told Space.com. She said that the seismic and infrasound data constrained the trajectory and acoustic energy, the video provided independent optical information, and the weather radar detected material from the fireball falling to Earth. "So, the real strength is that these systems provide different and complementary information," said Silber. "When a U.S. Government detection is available, civil data can independently validate it and add much more detail. When one is not available, as in this case [for Alaska], the civil networks can still provide a surprisingly complete reconstruction." The May 20, 2023 Queensland superbolide caught on camera by ground-based optical observations. These are selected frames from Australia's Paddys Green station showing the evolution of the event. Frame (a) displays the initial entry. Frames (b) and (c) illustrate the rapid increase in luminosity, leading to severe sensor saturation. Frame (d) shows the final stages of the trajectory. (Image credit: Elizabeth Silber, et al.) Independent view The Alaska study shows how valuable it is to put together diverse types of observations once an event has occurred, said Silber. Each measurement responds to a different part of the event. "Seismic and infrasound sensors record the atmospheric shock waves and can constrain the trajectory, fragmentation and energy," she added. "Optical observations provide an independent view of the luminous flight. Doppler weather radar can detect surviving material after it has slowed and entered dark flight." Bottom line: no single sensor tells you everything. "Combining independent observations lets us move from simply knowing that an event occurred to determining how the object traveled through the atmosphere, where it fragmented, how much energy it released, and whether material may have survived to the ground," said Silber. Artist's rendering of NOAA's GOES East satellite in orbit. The spacecraft provides real-time mapping of lightning activity, among other duties. (Image credit: NOAA) 'Hard rain' is gonna fall Researchers got pretty lucky with the April 1, 2026 event over the South Atlantic, according to NASA's Rob Landis, a planetary defense specialist: Two civilian spacecraft located at different locations in geosynchronous orbit allowed them to conduct a rather unique investigation of this bolide. "With two civilian resources, we can actually discuss things more openly," Landis, who's now a visiting vehicle integration manager for the International Space Station at NASA's Johnson Space Center , told Space.com. Lightning-watching instruments not designed for detecting bolides, he said, "afford the science community to discuss these events and these sensors in a forthright, open manner. These lightning imagers give us opportunistic bonus science for those who study the 'hard rain.'" Landis said that, in his personal view, there's a lot of smaller stuff getting through the atmosphere. "To the casual observer, these certainly produce wonderful natural fireworks and are mostly harmless," Landis said. But, he stressed, it's important to be able to distinguish between natural events and human-made ones. "It would be a horrific tragedy if any nation responded to a natural event — if they misinterpret it as a preemptive strike," cautioned Landis. Sandia intern Logan Scamfer checks data recorded by a ground sensor in Alaska. Scamfer works with Sandia physicist Elizabeth Silber, whose research focuses on using infrasound, a low-frequency sound too deep for people to hear, and seismic data to study meteors and other fast-moving objects in the atmosphere. (Image credit: Logan Scamfer) Real-world tests So, in the big picture, having collaborative, multiple and independent ways to observe atmospheric entries is of benefit to planetary defense thinkers. "Planetary defense is not only about finding an object before it reaches Earth ," Silber said. "It is also about understanding what happens during atmospheric entry — that is, how the object f

item.title: Watch Tunde Kelani’s Remastered Agogo Èèwò & Revisit the World of Saworoide
item.description: Official poster for Tunde Kelani’s remastered political classic, “Agogo Èèwò.” If you watched Saworoide , get ready to return to Jogbo. Tunde Kelani ’s political drama Agogo Èèwò (2002), the follow-up to his acclaimed classic, is now available in a newly remastered presentation on TK ÒPÓMÚLÉRÓ’s YouTube channel. Following the fall of military ruler Lagata in Saworoide, the people of Jogbo hope for a new era of peace and prosperity. But the corrupt chiefs have other plans. They install Adebosipo, played by the late veteran actor Dejumo Lewis , as the new king, believing that his background as a retired police officer will make him easy to control as they continue to exploit the kingdom’s treasury. Adebosipo, however, refuses to play along. Determined to protect the people of Jogbo, he demands accountability from the chiefs, setting off a fierce struggle over power, corruption and the future of the kingdom. The conflict reaches a defining moment during a public traditional oath-taking ceremony before the sacred Agogo Èèwò, or Gong of Taboo. Under the custom, anyone who has stolen from the land must confess before the gong sounds seven times, or face the consequences. Written by Professor Akinwunmi Isola and directed by Tunde Kelani, Agogo Èèwò remains a pointed examination of corruption, leadership and traditional systems of accountability. More than two decades after its original release, the film’s return in a remastered version gives audiences another opportunity to revisit the story and its enduring questions about those entrusted with power. The remastered Agogo Èèwò is now streaming on YouTube via TK ÒPÓMÚLÉRÓ. Watch below The post Watch Tunde Kelani’s Remastered Agogo Èèwò & Revisit the World of Saworoide appeared first on BellaNaija - Showcasing Africa to the world. Read today! .

item.title: Oleshky residents return to Ukraine
item.description: Residents evacuated from Russian-occupied Oleshky have reached Ukrainian-held territory following a rare local truce. They described years of isolation, food shortages and regular shelling, with some saying they were forced to eat grass and dogs to survive. Seized by Russian forces in the early days of the 2022 invasion, the city remains cut off by the Dnipro River on one side and Russian troops on the other.

item.title: On this day in space! Nov. 1, 1962: The Soviet Union Launches Mars 1 spacecraft to Red Planet during the Space Race
item.description: null On Nov. 1, 1962, the Soviet Union launched the Mars 1 spacecraft on a mission to fly by the Red Planet. While it did end up flying by Mars , the mission was not exactly a success. After it separated from the rocket, it deployed its solar panels and started cruising toward Mars. When mission controllers were checking out the telemetry it transmitted back to Earth, they found out that Mars 1 had sprung a leak in one of the gas valves that controls the spacecraft's orientation. And without a working orientation system, Mars 1 would have a hard time pointing its antennas in the right direction. It lost contact with Earth when it was about halfway to Mars . A model of Mars 1, a Mars flyby spacecraft launched to the Red Planet by the Soviet Union on Nov. 1, 1962. (Image credit: NASA) Why it mattered Ever since Galileo Galilei pointed his telescope to the red-tinted star and identified as a planet, Mars has captivated scientists' interests as to its nature. So it was of no surprise that as soon as we gained the ability to send missions into space, that the focus turned to the "fourth rock from the Sun." As it turned out, though, reaching Mars, let alone entering its orbit or landing on its surface,, was and continues to be difficult. Mars 1, despite its name, was actually the Soviet Union's fourth attempt at sending a probe to the planet. The first three ended in launch failures. Similar problems faced the United States, as well, but it was NASA's Mariner IV mission that became the first to successfully fly by Mars two years later. Still, as humanity continues to push forward to the day people land on, explore and live on Mars, the 1962 Soviet mission stands as the first to get close to revealing the first details about the planet. Want more space history? Check out our full On This Day In Space Story archive and watch our On This Day In Space videos on YouTube .

item.title: FBI says North Korea behind $6 billion crypto theft from Binance
item.description: Binance said Sunday that it had resumed withdrawals after more than $6 billion in virtual assets were stolen from the cryptocurrency exchange in a major hack the FBI said North Korea was responsible for. Binance is the world’s largest crypto exchange by daily trading volumes. News of the hacking attack, which is thought to be the biggest-ever crypto heist, caused the prices of most major cryptocurrencies to fall sharply on Friday. The company has offered reassurances it will cover the losses from the attack, saying it has used company funds to buy tokens to replenish 90 percent of what was stolen. Binance suspended user withdrawals after the attack but said they would be resumed in phases, the first of which began on Sunday. “First batch network now opened in phase one of withdrawals,” the exchange posted on X . The US law enforcement agency accused North Korea of being behind the hack in a statement on Saturday, confirming earlier suspicions from private investigators and analysts that a Pyongyang-affiliated group called TraderTraitor was responsible. TraderTraitor is the same group blamed for a $1.5 billion theft from the Bybit platform in February last year. “The Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) is releasing information advising the Democratic People’s Republic of Korea (North Korea) was responsible for the theft of more than $6 billion USD in virtual assets from cryptocurrency exchange Binance, on or about October 29, 2026,” the statement said. The FBI added that it had observed “TraderTraitor actors” converting stolen assets into Ethereum, and expected those assets to be laundered further by converting them using decentralized finance and instant swap services. It said it was urging private sector entities “to block transactions with or derived from addresses TraderTraitor actors are using to launder these stolen assets.” US President Donald Trump cast doubt on the North Korea’s involvement in the hack. “I’m not concerned. We’re learning about it. We don’t know if it’s North Korea,” Trump told reporters at his residence in Florida late Saturday. The president often reflects with pride on summits he held with North Korean leader Kim Jong Un during his first term. Binance has said that it was preparing to gradually resume withdrawals, starting at between 0600 and 0900 GMT on Sunday. “We are taking a phased approach by prioritizing tokens based on the past week data of user demand, so that each network and asset pair can be restored carefully, with stability and security checks completed before access is reopened,” it said. – ‘Cover the financial impact’ – Binance said Saturday it has set aside more than $6.34 billion in company funds to cover losses in the hack. “Our commitment remains the same: Binance will fully cover the financial impact of the funds stolen in this incident,” the company said on X. item.content:encoded: Binance said Sunday that it had resumed withdrawals after more than $6 billion in virtual assets were stolen from the cryptocurrency exchange in a major hack the FBI said North Korea was responsible for. Binance is the world’s largest crypto exchange by daily trading volumes. News of the hacking attack, which is thought to be the biggest-ever crypto heist, caused the prices of most major cryptocurrencies to fall sharply on Friday. Binance suspended user withdrawals after the attack but said they would be resumed in phases, the first of which began on Sunday. “First batch network now opened in phase one of withdrawals,” the exchange posted on X . The US law enforcement agency accused North Korea of being behind the hack in a statement on Saturday, confirming earlier suspicions from private investigators and analysts that a Pyongyang-affiliated group called TraderTraitor was responsible. TraderTraitor is the same group blamed for a $1.5 billion theft from the Bybit platform in February last year. “The Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) is releasing information advising the Democratic People’s Republic of Korea (North Korea) was responsible for the theft of more than $6 billion USD in virtual assets from cryptocurrency exchange Binance, on or about October 29, 2026,” the statement said. The FBI added that it had observed “TraderTraitor actors” converting stolen assets into Ethereum, and expected those assets to be laundered further by converting them using decentralized finance and instant swap services. It said it was urging private sector entities “to block transactions with or derived from addresses TraderTraitor actors are using to launder these stolen assets.” US President Donald Trump cast doubt on the North Korea’s involvement in the hack. “I’m not concerned. We’re learning about it. We don’t know if it’s North Korea,” Trump told reporters at his residence in Florida late Saturday. The president often reflects with pride on summits he held with North Korean leader Kim Jong Un during his first term. Binance has said that it was preparing to gradually resume withdrawals, starting at between 0600 and 0900 GMT on Sunday. “We are taking a phased approach by prioritizing tokens based on the past week data of user demand, so that each network and asset pair can be restored carefully, with stability and security checks completed before access is reopened,” it said. – ‘Cover the financial impact’ – Binance said Saturday it has set aside more than $6.34 billion in company funds to cover losses in the hack. “Our commitment remains the same: Binance will fully cover the financial impact of the funds stolen in this incident,” the company said on X. It said it has used company money to buy tokens to replenish 90 percent of the stolen funds, while the remaining 10 percent of tokens are “less liquid, which means they may take longer to source in the required amounts.” The attack on Binance came as many observers express worries that the ever-expanding capabilities of artificial intelligence models could compromise cryptography and IT security protocols. Bitcoin plunged nearly five percent after the news of the hack, while Ethereum dropped nearly six percent and BNB, native to Binance, tumbled nearly 10 percent. The sheer scale of the hack has put a spotlight on the capacity of North Korea — which faces extensive international sanctions over its nuclear and missile programs — to find illicit means to capture revenue. TraderTraitor is believed to be part of the Lazarus Group, which gained notoriety in 2014 when it was accused of hacking into Sony Pictures as revenge for “The Interview,” a film that mocked North Korean leader Kim Jong Un. item.title: PDP, NDC members defect to APC as ‘Tinubu Must Stay’ spreads to Jigawa
item.description: By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA: Some members of the Peoples Democratic Party PDP and the Nigeria Democratic Congress NDC have defected to the ruling All Progressives Congress APC in Jigawa State. They announced their defection in Garun Gabas Ward of Malam Madori Local Government Area at the inauguration of a grassroots campaign office for President Bola Tinubu, led by the Director General of the National Information Technology Development Agency NITDA, Kashifu Inuwa Abdullahi. Abdullahi and the Malam Madori APC leadership received the defectors who credited their decision to what they described as development interventions and improvements in their communities. They also singled out projects facilitated through NITDA, saying these had deepened their confidence in the administration’s development agenda. The event which was organised by the Tinubu Movement for Sustainable Governance Foundation TMS, popularly called the Tinubu Must Stay Movement, saw the llarge crowd of APC chieftains, community leaders, women, youths and other supporters chanting “Tinubu Must Stay” along the streets. Abdullahi, who is Chairman of the TMS Board of Trustees and National Coordinator, said the movement was taking its message to the grassroots ahead of the 2027 general elections and Tinubu’s anticipated re-election bid. “The essence of creating the TMS Movement is to go down to the grassroots level to enlighten citizens on President Tinubu’s reforms. He made it clear when he assumed office that economic diversification and inclusivity in attaining national prosperity are paramount to his reform agenda,” he said. He said the administration’s interventions in education, agriculture, food security, national security, digital literacy and healthcare were designed to stimulate economic growth and improve livelihoods. Abdullahi cited South Korea, Singapore, Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates and Malaysia as countries whose experience showed the importance of sustained economic reforms and policy continuity. According to him, Nigeria needs consistent implementation of development policies to compete favourably with emerging economies. “On this note, I implore the people to come out en masse and ensure a landslide victory for President Bola Ahmed Tinubu in 2027,” he told the gathering. The TMS National Coordinator also announced plans to empower another 200 women in Garun Gabas Ward. He said this would follow an earlier programme in Hadejia, where beneficiaries received financial assistance, sewing machines, bakery equipment, agricultural inputs and other support for small businesses. He said the movement would keep prioritising women, youths, children and persons with disabilities through economic empowerment, educational assistance and community development. They announced their defection in Garun Gabas Ward of Malam Madori Local Government Area at the inauguration of a grassroots campaign office for President Bola Tinubu, led by the Director General of the National Information Technology Development Agency NITDA, Kashifu Inuwa Abdullahi. Abdullahi and the Malam Madori APC leadership received the defectors who credited their decision to what they described as development interventions and improvements in their communities. They also singled out projects facilitated through NITDA, saying these had deepened their confidence in the administration’s development agenda. The event which was organised by the Tinubu Movement for Sustainable Governance Foundation TMS, popularly called the Tinubu Must Stay Movement, saw the llarge crowd of APC chieftains, community leaders, women, youths and other supporters chanting “Tinubu Must Stay” along the streets. Abdullahi, who is Chairman of the TMS Board of Trustees and National Coordinator, said the movement was taking its message to the grassroots ahead of the 2027 general elections and Tinubu’s anticipated re-election bid. “The essence of creating the TMS Movement is to go down to the grassroots level to enlighten citizens on President Tinubu’s reforms. He made it clear when he assumed office that economic diversification and inclusivity in attaining national prosperity are paramount to his reform agenda,” he said. He said the administration’s interventions in education, agriculture, food security, national security, digital literacy and healthcare were designed to stimulate economic growth and improve livelihoods. Abdullahi cited South Korea, Singapore, Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates and Malaysia as countries whose experience showed the importance of sustained economic reforms and policy continuity. According to him, Nigeria needs consistent implementation of development policies to compete favourably with emerging economies. “On this note, I implore the people to come out en masse and ensure a landslide victory for President Bola Ahmed Tinubu in 2027,” he told the gathering. The TMS National Coordinator also announced plans to empower another 200 women in Garun Gabas Ward. He said this would follow an earlier programme in Hadejia, where beneficiaries received financial assistance, sewing machines, bakery equipment, agricultural inputs and other support for small businesses. He said the movement would keep prioritising women, youths, children and persons with disabilities through economic empowerment, educational assistance and community development. The APC Chairman in Malam Madori Local Government Area, Alhaji Tanko Ahmad, commended Abdullahi for facilitating digital infrastructure projects that have widened educational opportunities for young people. He highlighted the Information and Communication Technology (ICT) Development Centre at Government Secondary School, Garun Gabas, which he described as a significant boost to digital literacy. Ahmad pledged continued support for the TMS initiative and assured that party structures in the area would intensify grassroots mobilisation ahead of the 2027 elections. The TMS Convener in Garun Gabas, Engineer Hashim Suleiman, described the turnout as evidence of growing grassroots acceptance of the movement. He expressed confidence in the administration’s economic direction, citing developments in the financial and petroleum sectors as signs of improving prospects for investment and growth. He urged beneficiaries of the empowerment programmes to use the assistance productively to build sustainable businesses. “As you know, the movement started some weeks ago. We started from the UK, launched it in Abuja, and now we are here at the community ward level. This is just the beginning, as more grassroots engagements are expected,” he said. item.title: North Korea linked to massive Binance crypto heist
item.description: The FBI says North Korea was behind the massive $6.3 billion crypto heist that hit Binance on October 29th. item.title: Nigeria woos Russian investors, seeks local currency trade settlement at Moscow summit
item.description: ‎By Boluwaji Obahopo ‎ ‎Nigeria has called for a shift in its relations with Russia from political commitments to practical economic cooperation, urging Russian investors to explore opportunities in the country’s energy, solid minerals, agriculture, manufacturing, pharmaceuticals and digital sectors. ‎ ‎The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs, Ambassador Sola Enikanolaiye, made the call while delivering Nigeria’s statement at the Third Russia-Africa Summit at the Grand Kremlin Palace, where he also advocated stronger trade and financial arrangements, including independent local currency settlement mechanisms between both countries. ‎ ‎Enikanolaiye, who led Nigeria’s delegation to the summit, said the future of Africa- Russia relations must be measured by tangible economic outcomes, stressing the need to translate longstanding diplomatic ties into investments, technology transfer and development partnerships. ‎ ‎He said Nigeria was particularly interested in strengthening cross-border payment arrangements with Russia through mutually agreed systems, alongside improved banking channels and financial infrastructure to facilitate trade and investment. ‎ ‎The minister, who conveyed President Bola Ahmed Tinubu’s greetings to Russian President Vladimir Putin and the African Union Chairman, President Evariste Ndayishimiye of Burundi, said the private sector must play a greater role in driving the partnership. ‎ ‎He urged Russia to collaborate with African countries on commercially viable infrastructure projects covering railways, ports, energy, telecommunications, transport and logistics, noting that such investments would strengthen regional connectivity and support the objectives of the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA). ‎ ‎On the digital economy, Enikanolaiye warned against Africa becoming merely a consumer of imported technology, calling for expanded cooperation in artificial intelligence, cybersecurity, software development, digital infrastructure and joint research. ‎ ‎He said such partnerships should prioritise technology transfer, capacity building and the development of indigenous technological capabilities across the continent. ‎ ‎The minister also identified agriculture and food security as critical areas for cooperation, urging Russia to support African countries in expanding domestic food production, fertiliser availability, irrigation, mechanisation, agricultural research, storage and agro-processing. ‎ ‎According to him, recent disruptions to global supply chains have exposed
