item.content:encoded: ‎By Boluwaji Obahopo ‎ ‎Nigeria has called for a shift in its relations with Russia from political commitments to practical economic cooperation, urging Russian investors to explore opportunities in the country’s energy, solid minerals, agriculture, manufacturing, pharmaceuticals and digital sectors. ‎ ‎The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs, Ambassador Sola Enikanolaiye, made the call while delivering Nigeria’s statement at the Third Russia-Africa Summit at the Grand Kremlin Palace, where he also advocated stronger trade and financial arrangements, including independent local currency settlement mechanisms between both countries. ‎ ‎Enikanolaiye, who led Nigeria’s delegation to the summit, said the future of Africa- Russia relations must be measured by tangible economic outcomes, stressing the need to translate longstanding diplomatic ties into investments, technology transfer and development partnerships. ‎ ‎He said Nigeria was particularly interested in strengthening cross-border payment arrangements with Russia through mutually agreed systems, alongside improved banking channels and financial infrastructure to facilitate trade and investment. ‎ ‎The minister, who conveyed President Bola Ahmed Tinubu’s greetings to Russian President Vladimir Putin and the African Union Chairman, President Evariste Ndayishimiye of Burundi, said the private sector must play a greater role in driving the partnership. ‎ ‎He urged Russia to collaborate with African countries on commercially viable infrastructure projects covering railways, ports, energy, telecommunications, transport and logistics, noting that such investments would strengthen regional connectivity and support the objectives of the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA). ‎ ‎On the digital economy, Enikanolaiye warned against Africa becoming merely a consumer of imported technology, calling for expanded cooperation in artificial intelligence, cybersecurity, software development, digital infrastructure and joint research. ‎ ‎He said such partnerships should prioritise technology transfer, capacity building and the development of indigenous technological capabilities across the continent. ‎ ‎The minister also identified agriculture and food security as critical areas for cooperation, urging Russia to support African countries in expanding domestic food production, fertiliser availability, irrigation, mechanisation, agricultural research, storage and agro-processing. ‎ ‎According to him, recent disruptions to global supply chains have exposed the vulnerability of food systems, making it imperative for African countries to strengthen domestic production and retain more value from their agricultural resources. ‎ ‎On security, Enikanolaiye reaffirmed Nigeria’s commitment to peace and stability in Africa, identifying terrorism, violent extremism, transnational organised crime, arms trafficking, piracy and cybercrime as threats requiring coordinated regional and international responses. ‎ ‎He, however, stressed that such partnerships must be anchored on African ownership and African-led solutions, with external cooperation strengthening existing regional mechanisms, including the African Union and ECOWAS. ‎ ‎The minister further reiterated Nigeria’s commitment to sovereign equality, territorial integrity, non-interference and the peaceful settlement of disputes, while calling for reforms of the United Nations Security Council and international financial architecture to guarantee Africa’s rightful representation. ‎ ‎On the outcome of the summit, Enikanolaiye said Nigeria supported the adoption of a focused Africa-Russia Action Plan for 2027–2029, with clear priorities, financing arrangements and monitoring mechanisms to ensure that agreements translated into measurable results. ‎ ‎He specifically invited Russian businesses to take advantage of Nigeria’s position as Africa’s largest market and a strategic gateway to West Africa and the AfCFTA, highlighting opportunities in energy, including renewable and nuclear technology, solid minerals, agriculture, manufacturing, pharmaceuticals, defence and digital services. ‎ ‎The minister also said the summit had reinforced the longstanding friendly relations between Nigeria and Russia, recalling Moscow’s historic support for Nigeria’s unity, sovereignty and territorial integrity dating back to the Soviet era. ‎ ‎Speaking at the plenary session, Putin described Russia and Africa as natural allies in building a just multipolar world order, reaffirming his country’s commitment to sovereign equality, expanded diplomatic engagement, security cooperation and greater African representation in global institutions. ‎ ‎Similarly, Ndayishimiye stressed that Africa would not exchange one form of subordination for another, insisting that the continent’s international partnerships must respect its independence and development priorities. ‎ ‎He said the 2027–2029 Action Plan would provide an opportunity to address infrastructure deficits through technology transfer and skills development, while moving Africa from dependence on external assistance towards greater economic independence. ‎ ‎The AU chairman also identified water security as a major priority of the continental body’s 2026 agenda. ‎ ‎These was item.title: Hemp strikes back as Manchester City edge out London City Lionesses in thriller
item.description: Goals from Khadija Shaw and ­Lauren Hemp helped Manchester City to escape from Bromley with three points after a thrilling encounter with London City Lionesses. It was a statement performance from the home team, despite the defeat ­delivering a blow to any title ambitions they may have been quietly holding on to before kick-off. The gap between the hosts and the champions is now six points, after Hemp restored City’s lead ­following Jana Fernández’s equaliser. But that London City had even played their way into conversations about this season’s title contenders in their second season has been impressive. Continue reading...

item.title: Betta Edu courts 500 C’River women, sets 1.5m vote target for Tinubu
item.description: Former Minister of Humanitarian Affairs and Poverty Reduction, Dr Betta Edu, has set a target of 1.5 million votes from Cross River for President Bola Tinubu, come 2027 general elections. Edu, Co-Chairman of the All Progressives Congress (APC) Women Mobilisation Directorate, made the declaration on Sunday in Calabar, during an empowerment programme that benefited about 500 market women, petty traders and artisans. She said the initiative organised at the instance of the First Lady, Oluremi Tinubu, was designed to improve women’s economic livelihood, and strengthen grassroots mobilisation. She said the beneficiaries received N50,000 each, alongside business and household equipment, including deep freezers, blenders, and toasters. According to her, the intervention targets petty traders whose businesses are constrained by inadequate capital. “Some of them are selling trays that have just N5,000 worth of things on them, while some of them have trays with just N10,000 worth of items on them. “So we are giving these sets of petty traders N50,000 each so that they can expand that their business, build on it, so things can get better for them and their children,” she said. Edu urged residents of the state to support Tinubu, Gov. Bassey Otu and other APC candidates as the party was banking on grassroots women’s mobilisation to strengthen its electoral fortunes in the state. She expressed confidence that the state would deliver more than 1.5 million votes for the ruling party, adding that the directorate was establishing support structures for women across the country. She disclosed that the empowerment programme would be extended to other parts of Cross River, with Abi Local Government Area scheduled to benefit in November or December, while the northern senatorial district would be reached in January. The former minister also highlighted some Federal Government interventions, including the student loan scheme and free maternal healthcare, as measures aimed at improving the welfare of Nigerians. As part of the mobilisation activities, she led members of the directorate on a visit to the General Hospital, Calabar, where they interacted with patients, pregnant women and children receiving treatment and offered financial and emotional support. She said the hospital outreach was undertaken at the instance of the First Lady ahead of the APC rally scheduled to hold in Calabar on Monday. Edu also cited subsidised dialysis services and free maternal healthcare as interventions aimed at improving healthcare access and reducing maternal mortality. One of the beneficiaries, Esther Bassey, a widow from Odukpani Local Government Area, expressed appreciation for the support, saying previous empowerment programmes had helped her cater for her three children. Bassey pledged her support for the APC in 2027, saying she and her family would vote for the party The post Betta Edu courts 500 C’River women, sets 1.5m vote target for Tinubu appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: ‎2027: Promote peace, policies, not personal attacks – PDP tells supporters
item.description: By Muhammad Inuwa Dutse ‎ ‎The Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) in Jigawa State has urged its social media supporters to promote peaceful political engagement, issue-based campaigns and policy discussions rather than engage in insults and personal attacks ahead of the 2027 general elections. ‎ ‎The party’s governorship candidate, Mustapha Sule Lamido, made the call during a meeting with PDP social media users and political commentators in the state. ‎ ‎Lamido urged the supporters to use their platforms responsibly by promoting the party’s programmes, policies and candidates through constructive engagement. ‎ ‎He stressed that political campaigns should be driven by ideas and policies capable of winning public confidence, rather than abusive language and personal attacks. ‎ ‎”Political campaigns should focus on issues, policies and programmes that can convince the electorate, not insults or attacks on individuals,” Lamido said. ‎ ‎According to him, the meeting was organised to sensitise youths on the importance of responsible political communication and their role in promoting the party ahead of the 2027 elections. ‎ ‎He further disclosed that the party had completed arrangements to commence its campaign activities across Jigawa State. ‎ ‎Lamido reaffirmed the PDP’s commitment to conducting peaceful and orderly campaign tours across the state, without violence or unnecessary provocation. ‎ ‎”We are committed to peaceful campaigns across Jigawa State, and we urge our supporters to avoid anything that could create tension or disrupt public peace,” he said. ‎ ‎The governorship candidate also expressed appreciation to the people of Jigawa State for their continued support for the PDP, urging them to sustain their confidence in the party. The post ‎2027: Promote peace, policies, not personal attacks – PDP tells supporters appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: French School Blockades To Restart From Monday – Student Group
item.description: The head of a student group said a campaign of high school blockades would restart from Monday, adding the government’s proposals did not go far enough. On Saturday, hundreds of thousands of people, including high school and university students, took to the streets across France for a third consecutive weekend of protests. Some high schools will be blockaded from Monday, when students return from a two-week holiday, said Pierre Sourzat, head of the “Lyceens!” group. “It will be more significant from Tuesday, but we know that some schools will be blocked as early as tomorrow,” he told broadcaster RMC on Sunday. “We support all our comrades who are blocking their schools from tomorrow,” he added. A protester throws a smoke flare towards French gendarmes during a demonstration to protest against the “high cost of living”, in Bordeaux, southwestern France, on October 17, 2026 as part of a nationwide call for mobilisation bringing together various groups expressing their anger: former “Yellow Vest”, secondary school and university students, climate activists and even farmers. (Photo by CHRISTOPHE ARCHAMBAULT / AFP) France’s protest movement against soaring prices emerged from weeks of demonstrations by high school students protesting deteriorating learning conditions and inequality. On Monday, the government announced a series of measures aimed at addressing student protesters’ demands, including replacing the university admissions platform and providing loans for school renovations. Students said the proposals did not go far enough. On Saturday, Sabrine Kharbach, spokeswoman for the Union Etudiante (Student Union), said blockades of universities and high schools would take place on Tuesday and Thursday. President Emmanuel Macron has called for classes to resume in a calm manner, arguing that “young people have been heard”. Sourzat countered that “the president hasn’t listened to us”. “It’s smoke and mirrors,” he said. “There’s a bit of polish on the surface, but once you scratch beneath it, there’s nothing there.” Sourzat said the proposed overhaul of the university admissions platform, long criticised for its lack of transparency, failed to address the shortage of places in higher education. He also dismissed the government’s plan to reduce class sizes as insufficient, noting that it would apply only to 10th-grade classes. “We were asking for all year groups,” he said. With the eurozone’s second-largest economy on the brink of recession and under pressure to rein in its debt, the government has limited scope to appease student protesters through additional spending. The post French School Blockades To Restart From Monday – Student Group appeared first on Channels Television .

item.title: Delta HOSTCOM clarifies position on DESOPADEC publication
item.description: ….Urges workers, management to await court ruling on 30% payment dispute By Chiamaka Ekwuwe WARRI — The Delta State chapter of the Host Communities of Nigeria Producing Oil and Gas (HOSTCOM) has clarified that a publication criticising Governor Sheriff Oborevwori over the operations and funding of the Delta State Oil Producing Areas Development Commission (DESOPADEC) does not represent its official position. In a statement signed by its Chairman, Chief Comrade Sunday Ndidi Enujeke, and Secretary, High Comrade Joseph Lamienghan, the organisation said it had not adopted or endorsed the publication titled, “Oborevwori’s DESOPADEC Betrayal: Oil Communities Starved While Derivation Billions Vanish,” authored by Swill Mavua. The publication had expressed concerns about DESOPADEC’s funding and the development of oil-producing communities, while urging residents to vote against Oborevwori and the All Progressives Congress (APC) in the 2027 general elections. However, Delta HOSTCOM said the views and political recommendations contained in the article should be regarded as those of its author and not attributed to the state chapter. The organisation explained that its recognised leadership comprised Enujeke as chairman and Lamienghan as secretary, adding that official positions issued in its name should reflect the decisions of its leadership. It urged media organisations, government institutions, political parties, oil and gas industry stakeholders, community leaders and the public to take note of its clarification. DESOPADEC payment dispute On the dispute concerning the 30 per cent payment to DESOPADEC workers, the organisation appealed to the workers and management to maintain peace and allow the court to determine the matter. It stressed the importance of respecting the judicial process while awaiting the final ruling. Delta HOSTCOM also expressed support for the objectives of Governor Oborevwori’s MORE Agenda, which stands for Meaningful Development, Opportunities for All, Realistic Reforms and Enhanced Peace and Security. The organisation said sustained engagement between the state government and host communities was important to addressing developmental challenges, improving living conditions and promoting peace in oil-producing areas. It added, however, that its position on the agenda should not be interpreted as an endorsement of every government policy or a dismissal of concerns relating to DESOPADEC’s statutory responsibilities. According to the statement, issues concerning the commission’s funding, project execution, statutory obligations and workers’ welfare require constructive engagement with relevant authorities. It said environmental justice, infrastructure development, transparency, accountability and improved welfare remained important to the development of oil-producing communities. In a statement signed by its Chairman, Chief Comrade Sunday Ndidi Enujeke, and Secretary, High Comrade Joseph Lamienghan, the organisation said it had not adopted or endorsed the publication titled, “Oborevwori’s DESOPADEC Betrayal: Oil Communities Starved While Derivation Billions Vanish,” authored by Swill Mavua. The publication had expressed concerns about DESOPADEC’s funding and the development of oil-producing communities, while urging residents to vote against Oborevwori and the All Progressives Congress (APC) in the 2027 general elections. However, Delta HOSTCOM said the views and political recommendations contained in the article should be regarded as those of its author and not attributed to the state chapter. The organisation explained that its recognised leadership comprised Enujeke as chairman and Lamienghan as secretary, adding that official positions issued in its name should reflect the decisions of its leadership. It urged media organisations, government institutions, political parties, oil and gas industry stakeholders, community leaders and the public to take note of its clarification. DESOPADEC payment dispute On the dispute concerning the 30 per cent payment to DESOPADEC workers, the organisation appealed to the workers and management to maintain peace and allow the court to determine the matter. It stressed the importance of respecting the judicial process while awaiting the final ruling. Delta HOSTCOM also expressed support for the objectives of Governor Oborevwori’s MORE Agenda, which stands for Meaningful Development, Opportunities for All, Realistic Reforms and Enhanced Peace and Security. The organisation said sustained engagement between the state government and host communities was important to addressing developmental challenges, improving living conditions and promoting peace in oil-producing areas. It added, however, that its position on the agenda should not be interpreted as an endorsement of every government policy or a dismissal of concerns relating to DESOPADEC’s statutory responsibilities. According to the statement, issues concerning the commission’s funding, project execution, statutory obligations and workers’ welfare require constructive engagement with relevant authorities. It said environmental justice, infrastructure development, transparency, accountability and improved welfare remained important to the development of oil-producing communities. HOSTCOM outlines endorsement process The organisation said it would continue to engage its constituent communities through town hall meetings before taking decisions on political endorsements. It explained that such consultations would provide an opportunity for members to discuss issues affecting their communities and collectively determine their position. The leadership said: “HOSTCOM does not involve itself in campaigns. What we do is organise town hall meetings, which will kick-start soon. At the grand finale, that is when we normally endorse credible candidates, who must be delivered by the oil-producing communities across the 21 local government areas.” Delta HOSTCOM called for unity among oil-producing communities and reiterated its commitment to engaging government authorities and other stakeholders on matters affecting their welfare. It maintained that the disputed publication was not an official statement or political position of the Delta State chapter. item.title: Nigeria 2027 Election Watch: The Ballot Is Taking Shape, But The Political Ground Is Still Moving
item.description: Nigeria’s 2027 elections are approaching a particularly interesting stage. For months, the political conversation has been dominated by defections, coalition-building, candidate selection and arguments about which party controls which state. Now, another picture is emerging. The Independent National Electoral Commission is beginning to settle disputes over who can appear on the ballot. Political parties are still exchanging members and campaign organisers. And INEC is preparing to test the technology that will determine how millions of Nigerians are accredited and how election results are transmitted. Three developments over the weekend illustrate these different dimensions of the approaching elections. In Adamawa, the movement of politicians between parties has continued, this time with a group of APC members joining the Allied Peoples Movement. In Imo, the state electoral commission has postponed its local-government elections indefinitely. And nationally, INEC has published revised candidate lists, clarifying some disputed nominations while leaving others unresolved. These developments tell us something important. Nigeria’s electoral machinery is taking shape. But the political structures seeking to use that machinery are still changing. That is this weekend’s Political Signal. ADAMAWA: THE DEFECTIONS ARE NO LONGER ONE-WAY TRAFFIC Only recently, Adamawa appeared to be experiencing a major consolidation of political officeholders around the APC. Governor Ahmadu Fintiri had moved from the PDP to the ruling party. All 21 local-government chairmen and 226 councillors elected on the PDP platform subsequently followed him. For the APC, that represented an expansion of its network of elected local officials. Adamawa Governor Umaru Fintiri For the PDP, it meant losing the party affiliation of officials who had won office under its banner. But politics rarely moves in only one direction. On Friday, October 30, former Yola South Local Government Chairman Umar Barkindo announced that he had left the APC for the Allied Peoples Movement. He was accompanied by a group of politicians and supporters reportedly numbering more than 5,000. Barkindo attributed his departure to unresolved disagreements within the APC. The APM governorship candidate, Abduralman Haske, is also a former APC politician. The reported membership figure has not been independently verified. But the involvement of an identifiable former local-government chairman establishes that this is more than an anonymous claim of mass defection. The development complicates Adamawa’s political picture. The APC has gained elected local-government officials who previously belonged to the PDP. The APM is now attracting some politicians from the APC. And the PDP must continue organising after losing a substantial number of its elected council officials. But there is an important qualification. The local-government elections that produced Adamawa’s council chairmen were conducted by the Adamawa State Indepe

And nationally, INEC has published revised candidate lists, clarifying some disputed nominations while leaving others unresolved. These developments tell us something important. Nigeria’s electoral machinery is taking shape. But the political structures seeking to use that machinery are still changing. That is this weekend’s Political Signal. ADAMAWA: THE DEFECTIONS ARE NO LONGER ONE-WAY TRAFFIC Only recently, Adamawa appeared to be experiencing a major consolidation of political officeholders around the APC. Governor Ahmadu Fintiri had moved from the PDP to the ruling party. All 21 local-government chairmen and 226 councillors elected on the PDP platform subsequently followed him. For the APC, that represented an expansion of its network of elected local officials. Adamawa Governor Umaru Fintiri For the PDP, it meant losing the party affiliation of officials who had won office under its banner. But politics rarely moves in only one direction. On Friday, October 30, former Yola South Local Government Chairman Umar Barkindo announced that he had left the APC for the Allied Peoples Movement. He was accompanied by a group of politicians and supporters reportedly numbering more than 5,000. Barkindo attributed his departure to unresolved disagreements within the APC. The APM governorship candidate, Abduralman Haske, is also a former APC politician. The reported membership figure has not been independently verified. But the involvement of an identifiable former local-government chairman establishes that this is more than an anonymous claim of mass defection. The development complicates Adamawa’s political picture. The APC has gained elected local-government officials who previously belonged to the PDP. The APM is now attracting some politicians from the APC. And the PDP must continue organising after losing a substantial number of its elected council officials. But there is an important qualification. The local-government elections that produced Adamawa’s council chairmen were conducted by the Adamawa State Independent Electoral Commission, not INEC. Their results established who was elected to local office. They did not measure how Adamawa residents intend to vote in the 2027 presidential election. Likewise, the subsequent defections establish changes in the affiliations of politicians, not necessarily changes in the preferences of their constituents. The political structures have moved. Whether the voters move with them remains an open question. That distinction will become increasingly important as the campaign progresses. IMO: AN ELECTION POSTPONED, AN OPPORTUNITY FOR EVIDENCE LOST Another development emerged in Imo State. The Imo State Independent Electoral Commission has indefinitely postponed the local-government elections previously scheduled for November 7. The elections had initially been planned for September 26 before being rescheduled. The Commission says its latest decision followed consultations with political parties and the Inter-Party Advisory Council. No replacement date has been announced. The proposed elections would have covered 27 local-government areas and 305 wards. Their postponement means there will be no immediate fresh council-election evidence from Imo ahead of the general elections. But even if the elections had proceeded, their results would have required careful interpretation. Local-government elections conducted by state electoral commissions are not administered under precisely the same arrangements as INEC-run federal and state elections. They may tell us something about political organisation, local participation and the ability of parties to field candidates. But a sweep of council seats does not necessarily establish how the same electorate will vote in a presidential contest. Imo therefore remains a state where we must look beyond local-government party control when assessing the political environment. The postponement also raises a straightforward administrative question. When will residents have another opportunity to elect their local-government representatives? That deserves an answer independently of the 2027 campaign. THE BALLOT QUESTION: INEC REVISES THE CANDIDATE LISTS The most consequential national development is INEC’s publication of updated candidate lists following its review of complaints from political parties. The Commission received 130 petitions concerning governorship and State Houses of Assembly nominations. Of these, 66 were upheld and 64 rejected. The governorship petitions came from 12 political parties across 26 states. INEC accepted 41 of the 69 governorship petitions and rejected 28. For State Houses of Assembly nominations, 25 petitions succeeded while 36 failed. The Commission says its decisions followed consideration of complaints, party records and applicable legal provisions. This is significant because the controversy over nominations has now moved beyond arguments and petitions. INEC has made administrative determinations. And the revised lists show what those decisions mean for individual candidates. GOMBE: PANTAMI RETURNS TO THE LIST Pantami Former Minister of Communications and Digital Economy Isa Ali Pantami is now included in INEC’s updated list as the PDP governorship candidate for Gombe State. His running mate, Haruna Ahmadu Hasan, is also listed. This is a material change. Pantami had previously been omitted despite winning a court-ordered rerun of the PDP governorship primary. His nomination had been challenged by rival aspirants, including Khamisu Mailantarki, who questioned his eligibility under the party-membership requirements of the Electoral Act. INEC has now accepted Pantami’s petition. But that does not mean every legal question has disappeared. Pending litigation could still affect the nomination. For now, the correct position is that Pantami has obtained administrative recognition from INEC, subject to the outcome of relevant court proceedings. For Gombe, this clarifies the published governorship field without establishing any change in voter support. OGUN: ADEBUTU REMAINS EXCLUDED Ladi Adebutu, the PDP’s governorship candidate in Ogun State In Ogun State, the outcome is different. Ladi Adebutu remains absent from the PDP governorship list. INEC rejected his petition seeking reconsideration of the omission. That leaves the PDP with an unresolved ballot-access problem in Ogun. The party and its candidate may pursue further legal remedies, but those proceedings should not be confused with an administrative clearance that has already occurred. The implications are organisational and legal. The PDP must determine how to proceed while its intended governorship candidate remains unpublished. Other parties continue preparing for the election. But no conclusion about how Ogun voters will behave follows automatically from Adebutu’s omission. KANO: ADMINISTRATIVE ACCEPTANCE, JUDICIAL RESTRICTION Kano presents a third situation. item.title: Nigerians, other foreign graduates to get shorter UK work visa from 2027
item.description: The United Kingdom, UK has announced plans to retain its two-year post-study work visa for international students graduating from selected universities, partially reversing an earlier decision to reduce the duration of the scheme. Under the revised policy, graduates of universities with strong immigration compliance records and employment outcomes will continue to qualify for the two-year Graduate visa, while other international graduates will receive 18 months from January 2027. The UK government disclosed the change in its 2026 Budget, although it has yet to publish the list of qualifying universities or explain how institutions will be assessed. The policy introduces a two-tier system in which the university attended by an international student could determine how long they can remain in Britain after completing their studies. “The government will also increase the duration of the Graduate visa to two years for graduates from high compliance universities where there are strong labour market outcomes,” the Budget document said. The change comes after the government announced plans to reduce the standard Graduate visa from two years to 18 months for bachelor’s and master’s degree holders, effective January 1, 2027. Doctoral graduates will continue to qualify for three years. The development could affect thousands of African students, particularly Nigerians, who constitute a significant proportion of Britain’s international student population and rely on post-study employment opportunities to gain work experience and recover the cost of their education. Nigeria was the UK’s third-largest source of sponsored international students in the year ending June 2026, with 26,060 sponsored study visas issued to Nigerian main applicants, behind China and India. Nigerian nationals also recorded 20,604 approvals under the Graduate route during the period, making them the third-largest nationality group to benefit from the scheme. The Graduate visa allows eligible international students to work or search for employment in Britain without requiring immediate employer sponsorship. However, the visa cannot be extended, and graduates seeking to remain longer must switch to another eligible immigration route, such as the Skilled Worker visa. Students graduating before the end of 2026 can still apply for the existing two-year Graduate visa, while the reduced 18-month duration will apply to applications submitted from January 1, 2027. hile maintaining opportunities for international graduates and professionals considered valuable to the country’s labour market. item.title: Poland rocked by Constitutional showdown
item.description: Poland’s constitutional crisis deepened on Saturday as the European Commission urged President Karol Nawrocki to recognise new judges appointed by Prime Minister Donald Tusk. The standoff comes ahead of next year’s parliamentary election, with polls suggesting a close race between Tusk’s coalition and the nationalist right. Camille Corcoran reports.

item.title: Delta reduces inherited debt by N400bn, targets 2027 clearance
item.description: By Egufe Yafugborhi ASABA — The Delta State Government says it has reduced the state’s inherited debt from N463 billion to N63 billion and is targeting full repayment of the outstanding balance by the first quarter of 2027. The Commissioner for Economic Planning, Mr Sonny Ekedayen, disclosed this at the 2026 budget stakeholders’ engagement held in Asaba on Friday. Ekedayen attributed the reported N400 billion reduction to what he described as the Oborevwori administration’s prudent financial management and responsible use of public resources. He said: “We have been able to reduce our legacy debt from N463 billion to N63 billion. We are also working towards clearing the outstanding balance by the first quarter of 2027. “This achievement reflects the commitment of this administration to prudent financial management and responsible utilisation of public resources.” The commissioner said the state government would prioritise roads and other critical infrastructure in the proposed 2027 budget, citing their importance to economic growth and improved access to communities. He said the state’s expenditure structure currently allocated about 70 per cent to capital projects and 30 per cent to recurrent expenditure, adding that the government intended to sustain the emphasis on capital development in the next budget. The Asagba of Asaba, Prof. Epiphany Azinge, called for greater citizens’ participation in the budget preparation process, while commending the state government for its reported budget performance. Azinge said residents and other stakeholders should be given opportunities to contribute to decisions on projects and programmes that directly affect their communities. Meanwhile, civil society organisations at the engagement welcomed plans by the Delta State House of Assembly to introduce legislation regulating housing issues. They said appropriate legislation would help address challenges in the housing sector and provide a framework for improved regulation. item.title: From Nigeria to Senegal: Ibquake Performs at Historic Dakar 2026 Opening Ceremony
item.description: Ibquake performing live at the Dakar 2026 Youth Olympic Games opening ceremony. Senegal came alive yesterday at the opening ceremony of the Dakar 2026 Youth Olympic Games, with a vibrant celebration of culture, history and African creativity. Among the performers on stage was Nigeria’s very own Ibukunoluwa Aramide Ajagbe , popularly known as Ibquake , who represented the country with a spoken word performance. The ceremony took place at the Stade Abdoulaye Wade in Diamniadio, just outside Dakar, marking a major moment in sporting history as the first Olympic event to be hosted on African soil. More than 1,100 performers took part in the showcase, which featured music, dance, visual arts and spoken word. Senegalese music legends Baaba Maal and Kiné Lam , music group Daara J Family , Gambian kora musician Sona Jobarteh and social media personality Khaby Lame were among the other names featured. Ibquake on stage with dancers and the lit Olympic cauldron at the Dakar 2026 opening ceremony. Stepping onto the global stage in a structured white gown with a sculptural bodice and braided detailing, Ibquake performed against a backdrop of dancers in feathered and textured costumes. Her verses celebrated African identity, heritage and the possibilities ahead for the continent’s young people. Among the lines she delivered were: “We carry a flame for the African child to look beyond the horizon… We are both root and revolution.” Reflecting on the experience, Ibquake shared a personal message online about what being part of the historic occasion meant to her. She imagined her daughter one day asking when the Olympics first came to Africa, and how she would be able to tell her she was there. She wrote: “My daughter will one day ask me when the first Olympics games happened in Africa. And I’ll answer with speed and alacrity. She’ll ask me how I know… And I’ll say… Because mummy was a part of it.” Ibquake surrounded by dancers during the opening ceremony in Senegal. She went on to describe her life as a testament to God’s goodness and reaffirmed her commitment to telling African stories “Powerfully… Boldly,” adding that Africa will always be great in her eyes. The Dakar 2026 Youth Olympic Games run from October 31 to November 13, bringing together approximately 2,700 young athletes from 204 National Olympic Committees and the Youth Refugee Olympic Team. Competitions span 25 sports and 153 medal events, with activities taking place in Dakar, Diamniadio and Saly. item.title: Customs deploys AI tools to tackle fake news, online scams
item.description: By Godwin Oritse The Nigeria Customs Service (NCS) has begun deploying artificial intelligence and digital data-tracking tools to combat fake news and online scams capable of damaging its public image. The Comptroller-General of Customs, Adewale Adeniyi, disclosed this at the recently concluded NECCIPR Roundtable 2026 in Lagos. He was represented by the Service’s National Public Relations Officer, Deputy Comptroller Abdullahi Maiwada. Adeniyi said it was important for the Service to ensure that members of the public understood the reasons behind its policies, operations and enforcement activities. Speaking on the theme, “Algorithm Influence and Public Relations,” Maiwada said artificial intelligence had become increasingly important to Customs operations, including risk management and strategic communication. He explained that the technology was being used to assess risks associated with imported goods, classify consignments according to their risk levels and guide appropriate Customs interventions. According to him, AI can also analyse public sentiment and provide insights into how people perceive the activities of the Service. Maiwada said Customs was using available digital platforms to establish facts and working with other relevant agencies to identify and apprehend those responsible for spreading misleading information. He said: “The role of AI cannot be overemphasised, especially within our operations. Over the years, AI has been deployed in our core operational duties as well as strategic communication. “AI has also been deployed to aid risk management, which involves assessment of the risks in imported items so that they can be categorised according to their different levels of risk to enable appropriate Customs interventions.” Earlier, the convener of the NECCIPR Roundtable 2026, Nkechi Ali-Balogun, said the event was founded on the belief that public relations professionals should not only manage messages but also play a leading role in shaping national discourse. She said this year’s theme examined the growing influence of algorithms and artificial intelligence on public opinion and the flow of information. “When machines decide what we see, who is really shaping the Nigerian mind? Who now controls the flow of information that shapes what Nigerians believe? We live in a rapidly changing world, powered by AI, where a single algorithm can shape political narratives, throw out conspiracy theories, and dictate what millions read, believe, and share,” Ali-Balogun said. The post Customs deploys AI tools to tackle fake news, online scams appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Adeboye urges journalists to verify stories before publication
item.description: Says misinformation threatens public trust, clarifies prayer-walk photo, Tinubu comment By OLAYINKA LATONA The General Overseer of the Redeemed Christian Church of God, RCCG, Pastor Enoch Adejare Adeboye, has urged journalists and social media influencers to verify information thoroughly before publishing, warning that misinformation could damage reputations and erode public trust. Adeboye spoke at a monthly special thanksgiving service and prayer session organised for social media influencers, creative industry practitioners, content creators and drama ministers at the church’s national headquarters, Throne of Grace Parish, Ebute-Metta, Lagos. He said media practitioners and content creators had a responsibility to investigate claims before disseminating them, noting that unverified reports could mislead the public. The cleric used the occasion to address two claims about him that had circulated in the media. He denied protesting against former President Goodluck Jonathan, explaining that a widely circulated photograph of him in white and green attire carrying a placard was taken during a prayer walk in 2020. According to him, the walk was organised in compliance with an instruction from the Christian Association of Nigeria, CAN, for churches to hold prayer walks in their neighbourhoods. “It is true I carried a placard. It was a prayer walk. CAN said we should do a prayer walk near our churches. That is what I did in Ebute Meta. A walk is a walk,” he said. Adeboye pointed out that Jonathan left office in 2015, five years before the prayer walk took place during the administration of former President Muhammadu Buhari. “And everybody swallowed it and believed I protested against Jonathan. Nobody checked,” he said. He also faulted reports that, in his comments on President Bola Tinubu, he had said the President had “done his best”. Adeboye recalled speaking in the United States about the abduction of children in Oriire community, Oyo State, and stating that Tinubu, as Commander-in-Chief, had issued the necessary orders for their rescue. He said his remarks were subsequently presented as an endorsement of the President’s handling of the security situation. “Somebody then reported, ‘Pastor Adeboye said the president has done his best,’ and we all swallowed it. When I said the US should not bomb us anymore, that was not news. When I said the US should help us deal with the terrorists, that was not news. God have mercy on journalists,” he said. Recalling his undergraduate days, Adeboye said he took an elective course in the Mass Communication Department, where he was taught the principles of investigative journalism and the need to establish facts before publishing a report. He urged social media influencers to use their platforms responsibly and avoid circulating information that had not been properly verified. According to him, the walk was organised in compliance with an instruction from the Christian Association of Nigeria, CAN, for churches to hold prayer walks in their neighbourhoods. “It is true I carried a placard. It was a prayer walk. CAN said we should do a prayer walk near our churches. That is what I did in Ebute Meta. A walk is a walk,” he said. Adeboye pointed out that Jonathan left office in 2015, five years before the prayer walk took place during the administration of former President Muhammadu Buhari. “And everybody swallowed it and believed I protested against Jonathan. Nobody checked,” he said. He also faulted reports that, in his comments on President Bola Tinubu, he had said the President had “done his best”. Adeboye recalled speaking in the United States about the abduction of children in Oriire community, Oyo State, and stating that Tinubu, as Commander-in-Chief, had issued the necessary orders for their rescue. He said his remarks were subsequently presented as an endorsement of the President’s handling of the security situation. “Somebody then reported, ‘Pastor Adeboye said the president has done his best,’ and we all swallowed it. When I said the US should not bomb us anymore, that was not news. When I said the US should help us deal with the terrorists, that was not news. God have mercy on journalists,” he said. Recalling his undergraduate days, Adeboye said he took an elective course in the Mass Communication Department, where he was taught the principles of investigative journalism and the need to establish facts before publishing a report. He urged social media influencers to use their platforms responsibly and avoid circulating information that had not been properly verified. In his sermon, Adeboye described potential as a God-given ability bestowed on every human being at birth, stressing that no one was created by mistake. Using the bee and wasp as illustrations, he said different individuals could respond differently to the same opportunities, just as the two insects produce different substances from the same flower. He warned that people’s potential could remain dormant if they failed to develop and deploy it. “There are many journalists who could become world-class but will never go beyond their native towns because their potential was never activated,” he said. Adeboye urged those who had misused or failed to develop their potential to turn to God in repentance, saying divine mercy could help them fulfil their capabilities. item.title: 325 People Arrested At Palestine Action Protest — UK Police
item.description: British police on Sunday said they had arrested 325 people at a London protest in support of Palestine Action the previous day, ahead of a court appeal over the government’s contentious ban of the group. Demonstrators staged a “mass action” outside the US embassy ahead of the Supreme Court holding a two-day hearing from Wednesday on the UK government’s July 2025 decision to outlaw Palestine Action under anti-terror legislation. The United States also designated Palestine Action as “terrorist” in August, as the administration of President Donald Trump intensifies its campaign against left-wing movements. The British designation puts the group on a blacklist that also includes entities like Palestinian militants Hamas, and made membership of, or support for, Palestine Action a crime punishable by up to 14 years in prison. Pro-Palestinian activists and supporters stage a protest in support of the proscribed group Palestine Action outside the US Embassy in London, on October 31, 2026. (Photo by CARLOS JASSO / AFP) It has resulted in more than 4,000 people, including many senior citizens and Holocaust survivors, being arrested for showing their support for the group, according to campaigners and police tallies. “In total, 325 people were arrested yesterday,” London’s Metropolitan Police said in an update Sunday. “The vast majority of arrests — 320 — were for expressing support for a proscribed organisation under the Terrorism Act.” A smaller number of protesters also rallied outside the US consulate in the Scottish capital Edinburgh on Saturday, but no arrests were made there at the time. A pro-Palestinian activist holds a placard during a protest in support of the proscribed group Palestine Action outside the US Embassy in London, on October 31, 2026. (Photo by CARLOS JASSO / AFP) “Enquiries are ongoing to identify people seen wearing t-shirts and holding banners showing support for a proscribed organisation,” Police Scotland said in a statement shared with AFP on Sunday. “Evidence is being reviewed and further action will be taken as appropriate.” The post 325 People Arrested At Palestine Action Protest — UK Police appeared first on Channels Television .

item.title: 15 Years Ago, Zelda Told its Most Memorable Story with its Worst Gameplay
item.description: Hold the controller over your head. The Master Sword glows. Point it at the screen, hit Y to recenter, and swing. On the screen, Link swings… kind of the right way. Then, your chatty companion, Fi, chimes in with a very long and earnest explanation of something you figured out several minutes ago. Rinse and repeat for about 40 hours, and that’s Skyward Sword , one of the most cinematic, heartrending, memorable stories Zelda has ever told — and the one saddled with the most finicky gameplay.

item.title: NASA's Swift space telescope is about to crash to Earth. Where will it fall?
item.description: null NASA's Swift space telescope is expected to crash back to Earth in the next few days. The Neil Gehrels Swift Observatory will reenter Earth's atmosphere in an uncontrolled fashion, after a robotic rescue mission failed to boost the scope to a higher orbit. Swift launched to Earth orbit back in November 2004. Over the next two decades, it studied gamma-ray bursts — the most powerful explosions in the universe — and other cosmic objects and events using a trio of telescopes: a Burst Alert Telescope (BAT), an X-Ray Telescope (XRT), and its Ultraviolet/Optical Telescope (UVOT). On Oct. 20, NASA reported that Swift's orbit had decayed to 171 miles (275 kilometers) above Earth and that the roughly 3,300-pound (1,500-kilogram) observatory was no longer able to compensate for the effects of the increased drag. It entered safe mode, followed by Swift's operations team at Pennsylvania State University sending a command to the spacecraft that effectively ended its operations ahead of its destructive and fiery nose-dive. It's unclear at the moment exactly when and where Swift will plunge to Earth. But researchers definitely have their eyes peeled. A surge of reentries In physics fashion, for the most part, what goes up must come down — with more space hardware to follow. Thanks to the growing surge in low Earth orbit constellations and technology refresh cycles, there are 10 times more objects reentering per year than there were just five years ago, said Darren McKnight, a senior technical fellow at LeoLabs, a company that keeps a watchful eye on what's going on above our planet. "It is unfortunate that Swift was not 'reorbited,' but from a reentry hazard perspective it is a small portion of the stuff coming back in. The rub on this, of course, is that, while many people bemoan the reentry of more objects , I am much more upset about the rapid rate of abandoning massive objects above 400 miles [644 km]," McKnight told Space.com. Swift will likely disintegrate sufficiently upon reentry to not pose a ground casualty hazard, McKnight said. However, the internal workings of the observatory's X-ray and optical telescope might survive, McKnight said. Where in the world? Similar in view is Dean Sladen, a quality manager and aerospace engineer at the U.K. precision-components supplier Accu Components. "Once Swift falls to about 120 kilometers [75 miles], the end usually comes within a few minutes. The air in front of it heats up so much that the satellite will start to glow. Solar panels and antennas are typically the first to tear off, and at around 78 kilometers [48 miles], roughly eight times the height of a passing airliner, the main body breaks apart. Most of it will melt and vaporize," said Sladen. While it isn't yet known exactly where any surviving pieces will land, Sladen noted that Swift's orbit only passes over a band within about 21 degrees of the equator. item.dc:creator: Leonard David
item.content:encoded: null NASA's Swift space telescope is expected to crash back to Earth in the next few days. The Neil Gehrels Swift Observatory will reenter Earth's atmosphere in an uncontrolled fashion, after a robotic rescue mission failed to boost the scope to a higher orbit. Swift launched to Earth orbit back in November 2004. Over the next two decades, it studied gamma-ray bursts — the most powerful explosions in the universe — and other cosmic objects and events using a trio of telescopes: a Burst Alert Telescope (BAT), an X-Ray Telescope (XRT), and its Ultraviolet/Optical Telescope (UVOT). On Oct. 20, NASA reported that Swift's orbit had decayed to 171 miles (275 kilometers) above Earth and that the roughly 3,300-pound (1,500-kilogram) observatory was no longer able to compensate for the effects of the increased drag. It entered safe mode, followed by Swift's operations team at Pennsylvania State University sending a command to the spacecraft that effectively ended its operations ahead of its destructive and fiery nose-dive. It's unclear at the moment exactly when and where Swift will plunge to Earth. But researchers definitely have their eyes peeled. A surge of reentries In physics fashion, for the most part, what goes up must come down — with more space hardware to follow. Thanks to the growing surge in low Earth orbit constellations and technology refresh cycles, there are 10 times more objects reentering per year than there were just five years ago, said Darren McKnight, a senior technical fellow at LeoLabs, a company that keeps a watchful eye on what's going on above our planet. "It is unfortunate that Swift was not 'reorbited,' but from a reentry hazard perspective it is a small portion of the stuff coming back in. The rub on this, of course, is that, while many people bemoan the reentry of more objects , I am much more upset about the rapid rate of abandoning massive objects above 400 miles [644 km]," McKnight told Space.com. Swift will likely disintegrate sufficiently upon reentry to not pose a ground casualty hazard, McKnight said. However, the internal workings of the observatory's X-ray and optical telescope might survive, McKnight said. Where in the world? Similar in view is Dean Sladen, a quality manager and aerospace engineer at the U.K. precision-components supplier Accu Components. "Once Swift falls to about 120 kilometers [75 miles], the end usually comes within a few minutes. The air in front of it heats up so much that the satellite will start to glow. Solar panels and antennas are typically the first to tear off, and at around 78 kilometers [48 miles], roughly eight times the height of a passing airliner, the main body breaks apart. Most of it will melt and vaporize," said Sladen. While it isn't yet known exactly where any surviving pieces will land, Sladen noted that Swift's orbit only passes over a band within about 21 degrees of the equator. "That band is mostly ocean, though it also crosses populated parts of Africa, South and Southeast Asia and Latin America," he said. A diagram depicting the makeup of the Swift space telescope. (Image credit: NASA/Goddard Space Flight Center) Surviving leftovers As for which parts are most likely to survive and reach ocean or ground, Sladen pointed out that most of Swift's body is aluminum , wiring and electronics, which melt away early in the reentry process. What reaches Earth is usually small, dense and heat-resistant, such as titanium, steel and glass. "The most likely survivors are its six heavy reaction wheels, the spinning flywheels it used to aim itself, along with tougher telescope parts such as lenses and mirrors. Its mask of around 52,000 tiny lead tiles will almost certainly melt. Only a handful of small, scorched fragments are expected to make it down — nothing recognizable as a telescope," Sladen said. Sladen said that, at the current time, it appears that no detailed risk assessment has been published for Swift's fall. "However, this does not mean NASA has not done the work," said Sladen. "NASA's own orbital debris requirements state that the risk of human casualty from surviving debris shall not exceed one in 10,000, so it is highly likely this work has been completed but not published," he told Space.com. "Personally, I believe it should be published, as NASA has done with previous satellites. The risk is almost certainly very small, but it would give people a clear, factual picture rather than guesswork." A pre-launch photo of the Swift Observatory. (Image credit: NASA/Goddard Space Flight Center) Design for demise Sladen added that there's far more focus on how a satellite's life ends these days than there was in the past. "Many now carry enough propulsion to steer themselves into a remote stretch of ocean, or are built from materials designed to burn up completely, an approach called 'design for demise.' NASA and the European Space Agency limit the chance of anyone being hurt by a reentry to one in 10,000, and if a satellite can't meet that, it's expected to come down in a controlled way," said Sladen. So, should people be worried about having a nasty run-in with Swift leftovers? Sladen doesn't think so. NASA has said that harm to anyone on the ground is unlikely, and LeoLabs also describes the risk as very small. Most of the spacecraft will burn up, and any surviving pieces will most likely fall into the sea, he said. "The real concern is the long-term trend. With more satellites being launched than ever, the number of uncontrolled reentries is growing, which is why designing satellites to come down safely matters more and more," Sladen concluded.

item.title: Enugu APC urges residents to verify political claims
item.description: By Dennis Agbo The All Progressives Congress (APC) in Enugu State has urged residents to exercise caution when receiving and sharing political information ahead of the 2027 general elections. The APC Campaign Council’s Spokesperson and Director of Public Communications, Steve Oruruo, made the appeal in a statement titled, “Unmasking the Alarmism of NDC: A Clarion Call for Enugu’s Extra Vigilance.” Oruruo referred to public discussions surrounding the management of Amadeo Event Centre and a proposed town hall meeting involving the New Democratic Congress (NDC) presidential candidate, Peter Obi. He said the disagreement over the use of the facility was a matter involving the parties to a private agreement and urged political stakeholders to avoid drawing conclusions about the involvement of the state government without verified information. The APC spokesperson also called on residents to verify reports, particularly those circulating on social media, before accepting or sharing them. He said political discussions ahead of the 2027 elections should focus on candidates’ ideas, policies and capacity to deliver good governance. Oruruo further highlighted the development programmes of Governor Peter Mbah’s administration, expressing confidence that the government’s record would feature prominently in the electoral contest. He urged Ndi Enugu to remain vigilant, promote issue-based political engagement and assess the proposals and records of political parties as the state approaches the 2027 general elections. The post Enugu APC urges residents to verify political claims appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Dungeons & Dragons Turned Hansel and Gretel Into a Near-Perfect Adventure
item.description: Most of the published adventures for Dungeons & Dragons focus on epic fantasy , tasking players with fighting ancient necromancers, rampaging demons, or invading armies in order to prevent some great calamity. But the stakes don’t have to be so high to have a great session, and a bit of whimsy can prove just as memorable as a dramatic battle. That’s why one of my favorite adventures from Wizards of the Coast is a silly fairy tale inspired by Hansel and Gretel.

item.title: 'Mother of all editors' Emacs is 50
item.description: No lesser authority than the MIT Technology Review says that the Emacs editor has turned 50 years old. But then, it is biased — Emacs was invented in MIT's AI lab. Simson Garfinkel's article is simply called EMACS turns 50, but the sub-heading explains why it matters more: "How the MIT AI Lab's text editor gave birth to the free software movement." There are multiple timelines and accounts of the origins of Emacs, and it is not a single monolithic application. The name is an abbreviation for " E diting MAC ro S ", and the original editor for which this set of macros was developed was TECO – "Text Editor and COrrector," written by Dan Murphy in 1962. Murphy died earlier this year at the age of 83. The inimitable Jamie Zawinski has an encyclopedic Emacs Timeline – as he mentions at the start, his interest being that he long ago maintained a fork of GNU Emacs, originally called Lucid Emacs . It's still around, under its later name XEmacs. There are a lot of forks and re-implementations of Emacs out there, and we are not going to go into all of them, or this article would become a book – one only interesting to programmer-archeologists (to use a term coined by the late great Vernor Vinge ). As for who originally wrote those Editing Macros, though, another history has quotations from several of the people involved: On the Origin of Emacs in 1976 . (Note – some of the quotes still contain the | symbols that marked quoted text.) This credits Lisp boffin Guy L. Steele Jr with the original work in 1975, but in it, Steele says: "RMS is responsible for the names 'E' and 'EMACS'. RMS still deserves 99% or 99.9% or 99.99% or 99.999% of the credit for taking a package of TECO macros and turning it into the most powerful editor on the planet." Mind you, just a few years after the event, in a 1981 talk now preserved on the GNU website, Stallman said, "I began the development of EMACS in 1974 with an improvement to TECO". Like all the best FOSS, even in its very early stages, it was a collaborative effort – but around late October 1976 is when RMS took over the bulk of the development. Of the many forks of Emacs over its half a century of development, some are still just about hanging on in there. item.dc:creator: Liam Proven
item.content:encoded: No lesser authority than the MIT Technology Review says that the Emacs editor has turned 50 years old. But then, it is biased — Emacs was invented in MIT's AI lab. Simson Garfinkel's article is simply called EMACS turns 50, but the sub-heading explains why it matters more: "How the MIT AI Lab's text editor gave birth to the free software movement." There are multiple timelines and accounts of the origins of Emacs, and it is not a single monolithic application. The name is an abbreviation for " E diting MAC ro S ", and the original editor for which this set of macros was developed was TECO – "Text Editor and COrrector," written by Dan Murphy in 1962. Murphy died earlier this year at the age of 83. The inimitable Jamie Zawinski has an encyclopedic Emacs Timeline – as he mentions at the start, his interest being that he long ago maintained a fork of GNU Emacs, originally called Lucid Emacs . It's still around, under its later name XEmacs. There are a lot of forks and re-implementations of Emacs out there, and we are not going to go into all of them, or this article would become a book – one only interesting to programmer-archeologists (to use a term coined by the late great Vernor Vinge ). As for who originally wrote those Editing Macros, though, another history has quotations from several of the people involved: On the Origin of Emacs in 1976 . (Note – some of the quotes still contain the | symbols that marked quoted text.) This credits Lisp boffin Guy L. Steele Jr with the original work in 1975, but in it, Steele says: "RMS is responsible for the names 'E' and 'EMACS'. RMS still deserves 99% or 99.9% or 99.99% or 99.999% of the credit for taking a package of TECO macros and turning it into the most powerful editor on the planet." RMS is of course Richard Stallman, and the page also quotes some emails from RMS on October 23 and 31, 1976. Mind you, just a few years after the event, in a 1981 talk now preserved on the GNU website, Stallman said, "I began the development of EMACS in 1974 with an improvement to TECO". Like all the best FOSS, even in its very early stages, it was a collaborative effort – but around late October 1976 is when RMS took over the bulk of the development. Of the many forks of Emacs over its half a century of development, some are still just about hanging on in there. When we looked up the link for XEmacs, we were surprised to see that there was a new release: XEmacs 21.5.37 "lettuce" appeared just last month. And even the forks have forks: in this case, SXEmacs , last updated in 2020. Most of the changes in XEmacs and SXEmacs eventually made their way back upstream to GNU Emacs, which is still in active development, although as The Register reported in 2008 , RMS is no longer the primary maintainer. GNU Emacs 31.1 appeared in August. Cards on the metaphorical table: this vulture is not an Emacs user. We have tried. A major influence was one of the Reg FOSS desk's favorite writers, Neal Stephenson, who in 1999 published an essay called In the Beginning… Was the Command Line . (It was later republished as a rather short book, but the text is still online .) In it, he says: "In the GNU/Linux world there are two major text editing programs: the minimalist vi (known in some implementations as elvis ) and the maximalist emacs . I use emacs, which might be thought of as a thermonuclear word processor. It was created by Richard Stallman; enough said. It is written in Lisp, which is the only computer language that is beautiful. It is colossal, and yet it only edits straight ASCII text files, which is to say, no fonts, no boldface, no underlining. In other words, the engineer-hours that, in the case of Microsoft Word, were devoted to features like mail merge, and the ability to embed feature-length motion pictures in corporate memoranda, were, in the case of emacs, focused with maniacal intensity on the deceptively simple-seeming problem of editing text. If you are a professional writer–i.e., if someone else is getting paid to worry about how your words are formatted and printed–emacs outshines all other editing software in approximately the same way that the noonday sun does the stars." Emacs is 50-plus-year-old software, and it shows. This is a huge and complicated program: decades ago, the joke was that EMACS stood for "Eight Megs And Constantly Swapping". It is not an easy program to learn. Despite lavish documentation and a built-in tutorial, this is software so old that its terminology predates microprocessors and the personal computer. Its exhaustive manual is 804 pages long, and to pick some trivial examples, its terms for parts of the screen use “frame” to mean what’s now called a window, and “window” to mean what’s now called a pane. In the section on Keys , it discusses the Control and Meta keys. That’s a slight snag: you don’t have a Meta key, and neither do the authors of Emacs. It was a key on the now almost legendarily rare Space Cadet Keyboard, of which the Deskthority keyboard wiki says: “It is known as the holy grail of keyboards.” You can buy a modern replica, the Keymacs keyboard . They are hand-made in the Czech Republic, and depending on exactly what model and specifications you want, they cost from €2,998 for the Lispsaver up to €6,878 for the A624N Space Cadet . In other words, you can have a keyboard with a real Meta key if you want, but it is going to cost you. One of the problems with these historical terms, unfamiliar to anyone who wasn’t already programming in the 1970s, is that meanings drift. In the context of Emacs, "Meta" means Alt, or Opt on Macs . However, KDE also uses the Meta key – but what the KDE documentation calls "Meta " is the Windows key – or Command on Macs. Like most Linux folks, the GNOME documentation calls it the Super key. Names are important. They matter. Who's right, the Emacs folks or the KDE folks? Well, neither: nobody has Meta keys any more. We have Ctrl, Alt, and Cmd/Super/Windows. There have been valiant efforts to modernize Emacs and bring it into line with modern UI and terminology. This vulture tried to learn Aquamacs , which modernized Emacs with a native macOS UI, but sadly it's no longer maintained. Another, which we enjoyed trying, is ErgoEmacs , which changes the key bindings and rearranges the UI into something much more like the IBM Common User Access arrangement , as used in Windows and most Linux desktops. However, it never really caught on and you need to know your way around Emacs to install it and configure it for your regional keyboard layout. So complex is it to configure Emacs that there are multiple pre-configured distributions of Emacs, such as Doom Emacs , or the minimalist Emacs Solo . We wish someone did a "CUA-Macs" config, with ErgoEmacs integrated and able to pick up your existing keyboard config. Come to that, the Gershwin Desktop project that we mentioned along with GhostBSD last year is in active development, and it's based around GNUstep. Maybe its developers could pick up Aquamacs, and adapt it to GNUstep. There is a long history of such Emacs facelifts. One instance is Borland’s Sprint word-processor, one of the selling points of which was that it could emulate the user interfaces of most of the leading MS-DOS word-processors of its day (just before they all converged on IBM CUA). Before Borland acquired it, Sprint was called The Final Word , developed by musical equipment makers Mark of the Unicorn . FinalWord was based on an Emacs clone called MINCE . The Great Rival Another well-known Emacs distribution is Spacemacs , which adapts Emacs to have a more Vi-like user interface. Vi is the other seminal Unix text editor, as the Stephenson quote above mentions. As this article on Origins and the Evolution of Vi & Vim notes, it too dates back to 1976. Indeed, that’s the reason we chose the year in this story: Tilde, a text editor that doesn’t work like it’s 1976 . One feature of Tilde we enjoy is that it supports use of the mo

item.title: 5 bright planets to spot in November — when and where to see them
item.description: null This is a great month for planet watching, either in the evenings or mornings. During convenient evening hours, the planet of choice is Saturn , visible well up in the southern sky during mid-to-late evening hours. Telescopically, the southern side of its famous ring system is currently tilted about 6½ degrees to our line of sight. Around the middle of the night, Mars and Jupiter come into view above the east-northeast horizon and just before the break of dawn are in excellent position, soaring high in the southern sky in the vicinity of the Sickle of Leo the Lion. Watch how Mars approaches Jupiter early in the month, passes it on Nov. 16, then spends the rest of the month sailing away to the east. Meanwhile, in the predawn morning sky, Venus literally vaults into prominence as the month progresses. And from midmonth on through the end of November, Mercury asserts itself, appearing as a very bright "star" to the far lower left of Venus. In our schedule, remember that when measuring the angular separation between two celestial objects, your clenched fist held at arm's length measures roughly 10 degrees. Here, we present a schedule below which provides some of the best planet viewing times as well directing you as to where to look to see them Reminder: On Nov. 1 — where applicable — change clocks back one hour from Daylight Saving Time. On this date, the clock hour from 1 to 2:00 a.m. is repeated, thus making this day the longest of the year: 25 hours long. The mnemonic is: " Spring Ahead, Fall Back." Mercury Mercury, hidden during inferior conjunction with the sun on Nov. 4, will emerge in the eastern morning sky after the second week of the month to undergo an excellent morning apparition for the Northern Hemisphere. This rocky little world arrives at its greatest western elongation (20 degrees) from the sun on Nov. 20; its most favorable morning apparition of the year for mid-northern observers. From Nov. 16 to Nov. 26 speedy Mercury will rise in the east-southeast before the beginning of astronomical twilight, more than 95 minutes before sunrise. Venus Venus is a good reason to be up at the crack of dawn in November; it's a silvery lamp that rises above the east-southeast horizon. Venus was at inferior conjunction on Oct. 24. But the steep angle of the ecliptic at dawn in late autumn helps Venus vault noticeably higher with each passing day for observers at mid-northern latitudes. On Nov. 1, it rises 55 minutes before the sun. But just several days later on Nov. 5, viewers around 40 degrees north latitude can see Venus come up one hour and 25 minutes before the sun and shine 15 degrees above the horizon at sunrise. As November ends, Venus rises nearly 3½ hours before the sun and hangs nearly 35 degrees up at sunrise. All month Venus brightens impressively and on the penultimate day of the month it will reach the pinnacle of its magnificent brightness, shining at magnitude -4.9, rising almost 3½ hours before the sun.
